name: Durable release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: durable-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          persist-credentials: false

        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2

content.text:
Yes, I think full ID migration is the right call — and now that I've mapped it precisely, it's a clean, bounded change:

**In scope** (5 files, ~35 reference sites): rename `SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/B/C` → new IDs (renaming the files + their own `id` fields + their 22 references to each other), then fix up the 7 references in `SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json` and 4 in `SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.json`.

**Left alone**: `CODEX-RECONCILIATION-REPORT.md` and `CODEX-HANDOFF-RELEASE-TRUST.md` — these are dated historical records of a specific past review, not living references. Renaming the ID there would be rewriting what those documents actually said at the time, same reasoning as leaving the closed plan file's commit-message quotes alone.

Proposed replacement: `SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/B/C` → `SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-PERSISTENCE-001A/B/C` — "persistence" is the plain-English word for the actual mechanism (the plan survives as an explicit artifact across the plan-job/execute-job boundary), not an abstract quality claim. content.text:
This is a real, pre-existing bug — not something I introduced or missed in recent work. It's in code that predates everything from this session, and it's never been caught because **no release has ever gotten this far in the pipeline before today** (we already proved `execute` has literally never run in this repo's history — now we know why: `plan`, the step right before it, was silently broken too).

**Root cause:** `derive_release_commit_decision()` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:109`) re-derives the release decision by diffing the merged commit against its parent, and only recognizes a package's version bump as "authorized" if a changeset **directly names that exact package**. I checked all 11 consumed changesets — only `callisto-model`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto-cli`, and `callisto-vcs` are ever named:

```
filter-plan-by-report:    callisto-model, callisto-graph, callisto-cli
jolly-ravens-strut:       callisto-model, callisto-cli
release-pr-forge-commit-api: callisto-model
release-pr-commit-plan-cli:  callisto-cli
release-pr-staged-changes-vcs: callisto-vcs
... (rest are graph/cli only)
```

But `callisto.toml` defines a `[[fixed-group]] name = "workspace"` covering **7 packages** (including `callisto-changelog`, `callisto-conventional`, `callisto-fixtures`, `callisto-format`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-moon`) that must always version together — so those bump from 0.5.0→0.6.0 too, purely via cascade, with no changeset ever naming them directly. The validator sees their version changed with nothing in its `selected` set explaining it, and fails closed exactly as designed: *"A changed version without a consumed changeset is an unreviewed extra release."*

The check is doing its job correctly — it's just missing a whole category of legitimate cause. It knows nothing about fixed-group cascades, linked groups, dependency-driven cascades, or pre-release policy (the four `ReleaseInclusionReason` variants that `plan_version` already models when it *creates* the bump — this function just never learned to recognize them when re-deriving it from a commit afterward).

This needs a real fix in `derive_release_commit_decision`, teaching it to accept a version change when it's explained by cascade membership, not just a direct changeset. Given `callisto`'s own release will never pass `plan` without this fix, and it's genuinely a correctness gap (not a config issue on your end), want me to scope and fix this properly?

+            allowed_ignored_paths,

+        &self.canonical_root
+    }

+        &self.head
+    }
+

4	//!
5	//! These tests intentionally drive the compiled `callisto` binary over a
6	//! real Git repository. Registry and forge programs are replaced only at the
7	//! process boundary, allowing the test to assert the observable release

16	use tempfile::TempDir;

18	fn git(root: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
19	    let output = Command::new("git").args(args).current_dir(root).output().unwrap();
20	    assert!(
21	        output.status.success(),
22	        "git {args:?} failed: {}",
23	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
24	    );
25	    String::from_utf8(output.stdout).unwrap().trim().to_owned()
26	}

28	fn callisto(root: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Output {
29	    Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_callisto"))
30	        .args(["--format", "json", "--cwd", root.to_str().unwrap()])
31	        .args(args)

37	    std::env::var_os("PATH")

40	        .map(|directory| directory.join("git"))

42	            candidate.is_file()
43	                && Command::new(candidate)

45	                    .output()
46	                    .is_ok_and(|output| output.status.success())
47	        })

content.text:
PR opened: **https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/53**

Summary of what was found and fixed:

**Root cause**: `derive_release_commit_decision` (the function `release plan --from-release-commit` uses to re-verify a merged release PR) only ever recognized a package's version bump as authorized when a changeset named it *directly*. It had no concept of fixed/linked-group cascades — and `callisto`'s own `workspace` fixed group covers 7 of its 10 crates, none of which ever get named directly by a changeset. Every release has been failing here since the first correctly-signed merge, which is exactly why `execute` has never run once in this repo's history.

**The fix**: expand the authorized-package set using the workspace's existing `fixed_of`/`linked_of` group lookups, without re-implementing or re-running the full dependency-cascade solver — group convergence guarantees every member lands on the *same* target version, which is cheaply and independently verifiable straight from the commit diff. Added a new `E155` error that fails closed if a group's members ever *don't* converge (catches a tampered commit rather than silently trusting it).

**Bonus find**: writing the test for this surfaced a second live instance of the exact `rename_all`-doesn't-rename-variant-fields bug from earlier this session — `ReleaseInclusionReason` was serializing `group_id` as snake_case. Fixed in the same PR.

**Verified for real, not just in tests**: rebuilt the binary and replayed it directly against the actual commit that failed in production (`7444599d`, the run you originally flagged) — it now produces a correct decision.

Two unrelated things noticed along the way, not touched here:
1. `Cargo.lock` on `main` is out of sync with the manifest versions (still shows `0.5.0` after PR #51 bumped everything to `0.6.0`) — separate, minor drift.
2. Two throwaway spike repos from earlier still need deleting (`orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`, `-spike-public`) — I still lack `delete_repo` scope.

content.text:
Verified directly from source rather than memory: `changesets/action`'s publish step runs the actual `changeset publish` CLI, which iterates workspace packages and asks the registry "is this version already published?" — publishing whatever isn't. That's it. No git diff, no changeset-provenance check, no re-derivation of anything.

## How knope/changesets actually do this

**changesets**: Version-PR creation (what we researched earlier) computes bumps from changesets + linked-package config. Once merged, `changeset publish` looks only at the *current* `package.json` versions on disk versus what's on npm right now, and publishes the delta. It has zero awareness of git history, PRs, or changesets by the time publish runs — the registry itself is the only "already done" check.

**knope**: Same shape. It computes a release from conventional-commit/changelog state and publishes based on current versions, not by cryptographically re-verifying that a merged commit's diff traces back to specific authorized changesets.

Neither tool asks "does every version bump in this commit trace to something a human actually reviewed" — they trust whatever's in the working tree at merge time, full stop.

## Is Callisto's extra check necessary?

Two different questions bundled in "necessary," and they have different answers:

**Is *some* provenance check on the release-PR merge worth having?** Yes — and that part isn't in question here. Requiring a GitHub-verified signed merge of a PR whose branch matches the managed pattern (what we spent the last several days fixing) is a real, meaningful trust boundary neither changesets nor knope bother with at all. That stays.

**Is re-deriving the *entire per-package decision* from raw git diff, independently reimplementing cascade-expansion logic, actually buying something worth its cost?** This is the part worth questioning. It found a real bug just now — but notice *why*: it's a second, independent implementation of "how does a fixed-group cascade expand," built separately from the one in `cascade.rs`/`plan_version` that computed the *original*, correct decision. Two implementations of the same logic is exactly the kind of thing that drifts and breaks, which is precisely what happened. The fix I shipped teaches the second implementation about two of four cascade shapes; `Cascade` and `PreReleasePolicy` are still gaps by construction, and any future third cascade behavior will need this same treatment a third time.

## What we're actually trying to accomplish

Strip away the mechanism and the real goal is: **prove that what's about to be published is exactly what a human reviewed in the release PR — no more, no less.** That's a legitimate, valuable goal (it would catch a Callisto bug that made an extra unintended bump, not just a malicious actor). But the current mechanism achieves it the hard way: reconstruct the decision from scratch via git plumbing, using a second, parallel implementation of cascade logic that has to independently agree with the first one forever.

There's a comment already sitting in `release.rs` that says the quiet part out loud — `ReleaseInclusionReason` is deliberately "a model value... so every later process can validate the exact approved roster without importing graph." That's describing a **persist-and-verify** design, not a **recompute-and-hope-it-matches** one. The current `derive_release_commit_decision` never actually does what that comment describes.

## Proposed plan

Have the release-PR generation step **persist the real `ReleaseDecisionV1`** it already computed correctly (full `FixedGroup`/`LinkedGroup`/`Cascade`/`PreReleasePolicy` reasoning, computed once, in the one place that already knows how) as part of the commit — e.g. a `.changeset/.release-decision.json` sidecar written alongside the manifest/changelog edits. Then replace `derive_release_commit_decision`'s job with something much simpler: **read that file back and verify it matches the diff exactly** — every claimed entry's manifest+changelog actually changed to the claimed version, and nothing else changed. No cascade-expansion reimplementation at all; cascade logic exists in exactly one place, forever.

This is:
- **Simpler** — verification becomes a straightforward equality check instead of a parallel policy engine.
- **More correct** — automatically covers `Cascade`/`PreReleasePolicy` too, since it's trusting the *real* computation instead of a partial re-implementation of it.
- **Still strictly more rigorous than changesets/knope** — it still requires a signed, pattern-matched, human-reviewed merge, and still fails closed if the diff doesn't match what was claimed.
- **A real, separate change** — not a small patch. It touches the release-PR generation path (add the sidecar write), the commit-plan/forge-API executor (carry the file through, keep it out of the forbidden-paths list), and replaces `derive_release_commit_decision`'s body, plus its own spec.

I'd scope it as its own spec/plan rather than bolt it onto anything in flight. Want me to draft that spec, or talk through the design more first?

# Release PR: commit via GitHub API instead of `git push` (retire supersede)

## Context

**Problem.** `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` maintains the long-lived managed release branch by regenerating it from current `main` (`callisto version`) and `git push --force-with-lease`-ing it with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That token cannot push content that changes `.github/workflows/*` on a ref. Whenever `main`'s workflow files change after the release branch was cut, the regenerated branch differs from the stale one at that path and the push is rejected. Proven on this repo: run `33679599559` (2026-09-02) failed with `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission`. Today's mitigation (`workflowDeltaFromBase` in the snapshot -> `ReleasePrActionV1::Supersede`) closes the old PR and opens a SHA-suffixed one (#28 -> #48). Maintainer wants one stable PR and no PAT.

**Discovery.** `changesets/action` never `git push`es by default. `@changesets/ghcommit` `commitChangesSinceBase(force: true)` (its `src/core.ts` "FORCE UPDATE" path):
1. create/force-update a temp branch at the base sha (REST `git.createRef` / `git.updateRef`)
2. GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` on the temp branch, `expectedHeadOid = base sha`, `fileChanges { additions[{path, contents(base64)}], deletions[{path}] }` = only the generated files
3. REST `git.updateRef(force: true)` moves the real branch to the new commit
4. delete the temp branch (also on failure)

Their comment: "We cannot reset the branch and then commit because if the branch has an existing PR, GitHub will auto-close as it sees there's no changes with the base." The token never *creates* workflow content (new commit's parent is `main`, whose workflows are current; the ref move points at an existing commit), so the restriction is never hit. Bonus: API commits are GitHub-signed (Verified) and attributed to `github-actions[bot]` (PR #48's head `e823dd73` is currently `verified: false, reason: unsigned`).

**Unproven and load-bearing.** Nothing confirms the API path succeeds with the default token when workflows diverged. It cannot be tested from a dev machine (personal `gh` tokens carry `workflow` scope). Phase 0 is a falsifiable spike with a GO/NO-GO gate; no code ships on NO-GO.

**Outcome.** One stable `callisto/version-packages` PR updated in place indefinitely, no PAT, `Supersede` + per-PR `git fetch`/diff removed, Verified bot commits, version-PR job holds no git push credentials.

## Decisions already made (maintainer)
- Spike runs in a throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike` (created, used, deleted).
- `version-pr` checkout flips to `persist-credentials: false` in the same change (drop the zizmor ignore).
- One PR for model + CLI + action, opened only after spike GO.
- `setup_git_user` input stays accepted as a documented no-op for now (removing it is consumer-visible); revisit in a breaking release.
- Payload cap is a constant set from spike measurements (no escape-hatch flag).

## Phase 0: spike (GO/NO-GO gate)

Throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`, default branch `main` with `.github/workflows/spike.yml` (workflow_dispatch, input `case`, `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write`, checkout `persist-credentials: false`) and `.github/workflows/dummy.yml`. Setup: branch `managed` cut from `main` with a `VERSION` file + PR opened; then change `dummy.yml` on `main` so workflows diverge. Each case writes its result to the job summary.

| Case | What | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| A | regenerate `managed` from `main` locally, `git push --force-with-lease` with GITHUB_TOKEN | rejected (control; matches run 33679599559) |
| B | `git push --force origin <main sha>:refs/heads/managed` (git-only ref move) | rejected (confirms git-only alternative is dead) |
| C | temp ref at `main` sha -> `createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=main)` with `VERSION` edit, one deletion, a CRLF file, a small PNG -> `updateRef(force)` `managed` -> delete temp | success; PR still open; PR files == intended set; `verification.verified == true`; `commit.tree.sha == local git write-tree` |
| D | case C with stale `expectedHeadOid` | `createCommitOnBranch` errors (CAS confirmed) |
| E | additions of 1, 8, 32 MiB text | record first failure and error text -> `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` |
| F | case C twice with no change | PR stays open (no auto-close on reruns) |

GO: C succeeds with diverged workflows, PR stays open and updated in place, tree OIDs equal, D errors, E limit >= 4 MiB, verified == true.
NO-GO: C rejected with the workflows-permission error, or PR auto-closes -> stop, keep supersede, record evidence in spec 013's `revision_note`.
Record all outcomes in `PLAN-RELEASE-PR-API-COMMIT-015.json` `evidence`.

## Design

### Payload built in Rust, not bash (`callisto release-pr commit-plan`)
Spec 014 forbids policy in the shell; deciding additions vs deletions, refusing modes/renames/symlinks (which `createCommitOnBranch` cannot express), refusing `.github/workflows/` paths, byte-faithful contents (CRLF/binary must be read with `std::fs::read`, not the lossy `String` stdout of `CommandRunner`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs`), and size limits are file-semantics policy that needs unit tests. The shell does one mechanical jq mapping to GraphQL `FileChanges`, covered by the real-binary contract test.

`callisto version` already stages its writes (`git add` / `git rm --cached` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` ~440-470), so the index vs base commit is the authoritative change set.

Byte-fidelity invariant in the executor: `local_tree=$(git write-tree)` after staging must equal `gh api .../git/commits/<new_sha> --jq .tree.sha` before the real branch moves. Equal tree OIDs prove the API commit is byte-identical to what git would have committed.

### Types (`crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs`)
Replace V1 with V2 (snapshot is `deny_unknown_fields` and binaries can be installed independently of the script via `setup-callisto source: auto`, so this must be a real version bump; keep `Wire` + `SCHEMA_VERSION` check, `#[non_exhaustive]`, and `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"`):
- `ReleasePrPullRequestV2 { number, head_repository, head_branch, head_commit: CommitSha }` (drop `workflow_delta_from_base`)
- `ReleasePrSnapshotV2` (schema 2), `ReleasePrDecisionV2` (schema 2)
- `ReleasePrActionV2 { Noop{reason}, Create{branch, staging_branch}, Update{pull_request_number, branch, expected_head_commit, staging_branch} }` -- no `Supersede`, no runtime fallback (a shell branching on a 403 to pick an operation is exactly the policy-in-shell the spec forbids).
- `staging_branch = format!("{release_branch}--staging")`, deterministic so crashed-run leftovers are reclaimed; `managed_branch_shape` already rejects it (suffix not 40-hex) -> add explicit `ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` (E154). Keep accepting `canonical--<40hex>` so PR #48 stays managed and is updated in place.
- `verify_snapshot` now also catches a moved PR head (`head_commit`) -- the compare-and-swap surrogate before the non-CAS `updateRef`.
- New `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1 { schema_version, base_commit, message, additions: Vec<{path, contents_base64}>, deletions: Vec<{path}>, total_content_bytes }` built by `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes(base, message, Vec<StagedChangeV1>)`; `StagedChangeV1 { path, kind: Added|Modified|Deleted|Renamed|Copied|TypeChanged|Unmerged, new_mode: Option<u32>, contents: Option<Vec<u8>> }`; `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` from spike E.
- Errors (E141-E148 taken; `DIAGNOSTIC_CODE_SOURCE_FILES` in `crates/callisto-model/src/lib.rs` already scans this file): `EmptyCommitPlan` E149, `UnsupportedFileMode` E150, `UnsupportedChangeKind` E151, `CommitPlanTooLarge` E152, `ForbiddenCommitPlanPath` E153 (`.github/workflows/`, `.git/`, `..`, absolute, non-UTF-8), `StagingBranchPullRequest` E154.
- Dependency: `base64 = "0.22"` (MIT/Apache-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock`) in workspace + `callisto-model`.

### VCS observation (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` or new `staged.rs`)
`ShellGit::staged_changes_since(&self, base: &CommitSha) -> Result<Vec<StagedChangeV1>, VcsError>`: `git diff --cached --raw -z --no-renames <base>`, parse mode/status/path, read A/M contents with `std::fs::read`. Expose through `GitAccess` the same way `observe_git_commit_trust` delegates to the shell backend (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs:108`); nothing in `GitDataSource`/gix today lists changed paths or reads blobs, so this is new surface, shell-only. Recording-runner tests as in existing `shell.rs` tests (fake at ~:474).

### CLI (`crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs`, `commands/release_pr.rs`)
`ReleasePrArgs::CommitPlan(ReleasePrCommitPlanArgs { base_commit, message, out: Option<PathBuf> })`; `--out` writes via `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`, else JSON to stdout via `write_json`; update `render_decision` for V2 (drop the `Supersede` arm, keep the `_ =>` arm for `#[non_exhaustive]`); `verify` currently emits a hard-coded `{"schemaVersion": 1, "ok": true}` (`commands/release_pr.rs:31`) -- tie it to `ReleasePrDecisionV2::SCHEMA_VERSION`; update the `Decide` doc comment at `cli.rs:268` ("create, update, supersede, or no-op" -> "create, update, or no-op"; rendered in `release-pr --help`, not snapshotted). `help.trycmd` snapshots only top-level `--help`; refresh only if the `release-pr` one-liner changes. Add `release-pr commit-plan` to `tests/subprocess_dispatch_and_stdin_tests.rs` (`subprocess_lifecycle_exercises_every_main_dispatch_arm` does not cover `release-pr` today).

### Executor (`.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`)
1. `base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`; `snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)` -- `gh pr list --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid`; no per-PR fetch/diff loop.
2. `decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide ...)`; `case kind in noop|create|update`; read `.action.branch`, `.action.stagingBranch`, `.action.pullRequestNumber`, `.action.expectedHeadCommit`.
3. Compose body (unchanged).
4. `$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND`; `git add -A` (parity for custom version commands).
5. `callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-pr-commit-plan.json"` (empty plan is a typed error; replaces the `git status --porcelain` check).
6. `local_tree=$(git write-tree)`.
7. `trap` deleting the staging ref (`gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/<staging>`; tolerate 404/422 with `::warning::`).
8. verify #1 (`release-pr verify`, fresh snapshot).
9. staging ref at base: `gh api -X PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<staging> -f sha=$base_commit -F force=true`, fallback `POST .../git/refs` on 422.
10. `new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq .data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid)`; `body.json` built by jq from the plan (`expectedHeadOid: .baseCommit`, `branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner, branchName: <staging>}`, `fileChanges: {additions: [.additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}], deletions: .deletions}`).
11. `remote_tree=$(gh api .../git/commits/$new_sha --jq .tree.sha)`; require `== $local_tree`.
12. verify #2 (fresh snapshot; `headCommit` catches a moved PR head).
13. move real branch: update -> `PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<branch> -f sha=$new_sha -F force=true`; create -> `POST .../git/refs`, fallback PATCH-force if it exists (orphan from a failed run; no PR on it by construction). Then GET the ref and require `.object.sha == $new_sha`.
14. verify #3, label, `gh pr create` / `gh pr edit` (unchanged).
15. trap deletes staging (warn, never fail, on cleanup error).
Add `command -v gh` check; no `git push` anywhere in the script (guard in the contract test).

Residual race (state in spec): REST `updateRef` has no CAS; window between verify #2 and step 13 is milliseconds; the workflow `concurrency` group already serializes automated runs; the post-move GET catches a human push after the fact.

### Workflow / action metadata
- `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` `version-pr` job: checkout `persist-credentials: false`, remove the `zizmor: ignore[artipacked]` comment; permissions unchanged (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`). Line 116 (`release-candidate` job) keeps the `^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$` regex: historical SHA-suffixed branches (PR #48) remain trusted merge sources; `--staging` never matches it.
- `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh`: line 42 pins the exact `persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] ...` line -> replace with a `persist-credentials: false` assertion; line 27 pins the byte-exact `prs=$(gh api ...)` regex line -> unchanged.
- `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`: `setup_git_user` documented as no-op; `github_token` description no longer mentions git pushes; action description line. `justfile:36` comment mentions "supersede" -> update.

## Spec, plan, docs, changesets
- `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-PR-DECISION-014.json`: `architecture.execution` (materialize via forge commit API from a Callisto commit plan; staging branch; tree check); AC-002 drop "unless its observed workflow delta requires supersede"; AC-003 -> retained `--sha` branches + staging-branch rejection; new AC-006 `commit-plan` contract (parent is the snapshot base commit, no workflow paths, typed refusals, byte-faithful); AC-004 test list (create, update, retained replacement, noop, stale snapshot, moved head before ref move, tree mismatch, staging cleanup on failure, no `git push`); AC-005 schema v2; `revision_note`.
- `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json` AC-004 (line ~40): replace the SHA-suffixed fallback sentences with "updates the managed branch through the forge commit API so the built-in token never pushes workflow content; historical SHA-suffixed branches remain trusted"; keep "recomputes rather than rebasing" and "requires no elevated token"; `revision_note` cites run 33679599559 and the spike evidence.
- New `.claude/plans/PLAN-RELEASE-PR-API-COMMIT-015.json` (T00 spike with `evidence`, T01 model, T02 vcs, T03 cli, T04 action, T05 specs/docs/exit-gate); leave PLAN-014 as-is.
- `docs/06-publishing.md` lines ~15-25: replace the supersede/PAT paragraph (API commit, Verified commits, no `workflows` scope, historical `--sha` branches still updated in place). `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 9 input rows (`setup_git_user`, `github_token`) and line ~407 `release_branch` row ("GitHub-token fallback branches are created automatically when needed" -> remove). README release snippet unchanged.
- Changesets: `callisto-model: minor` (V2 schema, Supersede removed), `callisto-cli: minor` (`release-pr commit-plan`), `callisto-vcs: minor`.

## Tests (each phase validated individually before the next)
- Model: `derives_update_with_staging_branch_and_expected_head`, `derives_create_with_staging_branch`, `derive_rejects_pull_request_on_staging_branch`, `verify_snapshot_rejects_moved_head_commit`, `snapshot_v2_rejects_v1_wire_and_unknown_fields`, `action_v2_fields_serialize_as_camel_case`, `commit_plan_rejects_empty_change_set`, `commit_plan_rejects_non_regular_modes`, `commit_plan_rejects_rename_copy_type_change`, `commit_plan_rejects_workflow_and_unsafe_paths`, `commit_plan_rejects_oversized_payload`, `commit_plan_base64_round_trips_crlf_and_binary_bytes`, `commit_plan_serializes_camel_case_and_schema_version`.
- VCS: `parse_raw_diff_z_parses_modes_status_and_odd_paths`, `staged_changes_since_reads_worktree_bytes_and_marks_deletions` (temp repo).
- CLI: `cli_parses_release_pr_commit_plan`; `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_pr_commit_plan_tests.rs`: `commit_plan_reproduces_git_write_tree` (apply plan into a fresh worktree from base, compare `git write-tree`), `commit_plan_fails_closed_on_executable_bit`.
- Action stub test `test_release_pr_contract.sh`: stub `gh api` (record method/path/`--input`); cases create, update, retained `--sha` update, noop, stale snapshot before staging (no writes), moved head before ref move (staging created, real branch untouched, staging deleted), tree mismatch, cleanup-on-failure; keep the single `INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH` reference guard; add a "no `git push` in script" guard.
- Real-binary test `test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh`: V2 snapshot with `headCommit`; assert `.action.stagingBranch` / `.action.expectedHeadCommit` through the script's jq; temp git repo `commit-plan` run asserting the exact jq -> GraphQL mapping and base64 of a known file (this is the class of bug that shipped before; the stub test cannot catch it). Also remove its silent SKIP when `.changeset/*.md` is empty: build a temp git repo with a synthetic changeset and run `decide` with `--cwd` there, so coverage no longer depends on this repo having a pending changeset.
- Commands: `cargo test -p callisto-model`, `-p callisto-vcs`, `-p callisto-cli`; `just lint`; `just wasm-check` (model is wasm-built); `just test-release-action`; `just test-release-action-binary`; final `just ci-fast`.

## Verification (end to end)
1. Spike GO recorded in PLAN-015 before any code.
2. After merge to `main`: the next Durable release run must UPDATE PR #48 in place (branch `callisto/version-packages--567f321c...`), head commit `verification.verified == true`, no new PR, no closed PR, staging branch absent afterwards.
3. Deliberately change a workflow file on `main` (any real CI change) and confirm the following run still updates #48 in place -- the exact scenario that produced #28 -> #48.

## Risks / edge cases
- Payload cap unknown until spike E (today's full plan is ~150-200 KB base64).
- A future ruleset on `callisto/version-packages` blocking force pushes breaks `updateRef(force)` exactly as it broke `git push --force` (documented; none exist today).
- Custom `version_command` touching `.github/workflows/` now fails closed (E153) instead of being force-pushed -- intended.
- Rebase-merge of the release PR would drop the GitHub signature on the merge; the `release-candidate` job already requires a verified merge commit, unchanged.
- Staging cleanup failure only warns; deterministic name means the next run reclaims it.

skills.name: artifact-design
skills.content:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say "separate object" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

# Courier — PR

<overview>
Produces a PR title and body from a diff plus optional linked spec/requirement, then opens the PR. Delegates the narrative to `pr-narrator`; opening the PR is a visible external action and always requires explicit confirmation before the `gh pr create` call fires.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pr-narrator** | sonnet / medium | A PR needs a title and body a reviewer with zero context can act on. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`shared/references/github.md` — PR template, label conventions, `gh` commands, and the voice standard for this artifact (summary bullets first, test plan as a checklist).
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: git diff, optionally linked `spec@1` or `requirement@1`
**Produces**: opened PR (title, body, labels). Confirm the drafted title/body with the user before running `gh pr create` — this is a shared-visibility action, not a local one.
</io>
