name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
          # `just build` above is a workspace-wide debug compile-check, not a
          # shipped artifact -- nothing today copies its output into
          # release-artifacts/ (GitHub Release binary publishing has no
          # producer yet; publish-to = ["github-release"] is a documented
          # no-op in commands/publish.rs). This release build exists so that
          # if/when that gap closes, the CLI binary it wires up was already
          # being built in release mode here, not debug.
          just build-release
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

---
name: feedback_terse_comments
description: User wants code/config comments kept to one short line max; I keep writing multi-line prose comments despite CLAUDE.md already saying not to.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Stop writing multi-line prose comments in code and config (YAML, Rust, etc.). One short line, only when the WHY is genuinely non-obvious. This is already stated in the global CLAUDE.md ("Never write multi-paragraph docstrings or multi-line comment blocks — one short line max") and I violated it repeatedly in one session anyway (a multi-paragraph doc comment on a Rust function, a long CLI `--help` doc comment, an 8-line YAML comment) before the user called it out twice.

**Why:** User asked directly, twice in one session: "Do we need the giant comment or can it be succinct" and "How can I stop you from writing wordy prose every time?" — the second implies the first correction alone didn't stick and they want it to stop happening by default, not just get fixed after the fact.

**How to apply:**
- Before adding any comment, default to zero. Add one line only if removing it would leave a future reader missing a genuinely hidden constraint or non-obvious reason.
- This applies to inline/block comments (`//`, `#`) in the body of logic. It does NOT retroactively apply to module-level doc comments (`//!`) that are this codebase's established convention for architectural context at the top of a file — those are a different, pre-existing category the user hasn't objected to.
- If a comment is trying to explain a whole design rationale, that belongs in the PR description or commit message, not the file.
- When in doubt mid-edit, write the terse version first; only expand if truly necessary.

It does NOT retroactively apply to module-level doc comments (`//!`) that are this codebase's established convention for architectural context at the top of a file — those are a different, pre-existing category the user hasn't objected to.
- If a comment is trying to explain a whole design rationale, that belongs in the PR description or commit message, not the file.
- When in doubt mid-edit, write the terse version first; only expand if truly necessary.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
          # No debug binaries ship as GitHub Release artifacts.
          just build-release
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

input.prompt:
Read the currently staged git diff in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto (run `git diff --staged`) and produce a conventional commit message per shared/references/conventional-commits.md.

Context for your judgment (not to be copied verbatim into the message — the diff is the source of truth): this branch replaces `callisto release plan --from-release-commit`'s verification logic. Previously it re-derived the release roster from the merged commit's raw git diff by parsing consumed changesets and matching packages directly — which broke on fixed-group cascades (a sibling package bumped without its own named changeset). The new design has `callisto version --emit-decision <path>` persist the exact decision computed once at plan time, and the merge-time verifier now reads that committed decision back and cross-checks it against the actual diff (with digest-based tamper detection already provided by `ReleaseDecisionV1`'s existing Deserialize impl), instead of re-deriving policy a second time. Also includes: `ReleaseInclusionReason` camelCase serialization fix, CLI flag wiring (`--emit-decision`, `--decision`), GitHub Action script/workflow wiring for the new decision file, new adversarial e2e tests, and a `.claude/settings.json` permission allowlist addition.

Draft a PR title and body for the branch `fix/release-decision-persist-and-verify` in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto, to be opened against `main` on GitHub repo `orin-dx/callisto`. Get the diff yourself via `git diff origin/main...fix/release-decision-persist-and-verify` in that repo.

Context a reviewer needs (not in the diff, use for framing):
- Production bug: `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` (the function that authorizes a merged release-PR commit before real publish/tag/forge-release execution) used to re-derive the release roster from the merged commit's raw git diff — parsing which changesets were deleted and matching them directly to packages. This broke any release where a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling package that had no changeset of its own naming it (a fixed group unions all members to one target version the instant any member bumps) — the old logic rejected every such release as "stale."
- Fix: `callisto version` gains `--emit-decision <path>`, writing the exact release decision (package, target version, inclusion reason: changeset/fixed-group/linked-group/cascade/pre-release-policy) it already computed, committed alongside the manifest/changelog edits. `release plan --from-release-commit` now requires a companion `--decision <path>` and verifies the merged commit's actual diff against that committed decision (which already has digest-based tamper detection via `ReleaseDecisionV1`'s existing Deserialize impl) instead of re-deriving policy from scratch a second time.
- This is simpler and removes a whole duplicated-logic surface (a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution) rather than teaching the old re-derivation about groups.
- New adversarial e2e tests prove: (1) the original bug scenario is now accepted (fixed-group cascade with no direct changeset), (2) a decision whose claimed version disagrees with the actual manifest diff is rejected, (3) a hand-tampered decision file (digest no longer matches its own entries) is rejected.
- Also included: an unrelated but necessary serialization fix (`ReleaseInclusionReason` variant fields now correctly serialize camelCase via `rename_all_fields`), GitHub Action / workflow wiring to pass `.callisto/release-decision.json` through the pipeline, and a `.claude/settings.json` permission-allowlist addition (unrelated housekeeping, feel free to omit from the narrative or mention only briefly).
- This does NOT supersede any currently-open PR (there is no PR #53 in flight on this repo currently — it was an earlier abandoned approach in this same investigation, never merged, not part of this diff).

Write the PR body per shared/references/github.md's template and voice standard (summary bullets first, test plan as a checklist covering: per-crate test suites run and passed, clippy clean, the new fixed-group e2e test, the two new adversarial tests). Output the JSON object (title, body, labels, reasoning) and report it back to me plainly — do not run `gh pr create` yourself, I'll confirm with the user first.

content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

content.text:
Audit workflow launched in the background (`/workflows` to watch live progress). Design:

- **Scan** — 12 parallel agents, one per subsystem area (covering every crate), each hunting only for duplicate-logic and over-engineering, with full-repo grep access to catch cross-crate duplication (default model, high effort — this is the fanned-out step, kept cost-sensible).
- **Merge** — one Opus pass to deduplicate findings different areas surface from opposite sides of the same duplicate pair.
- **Verify** — adversarial single-verifier pass per finding, defaults to refuted unless the code itself confirms it (keeps false positives out of your report).
- **Synthesize** — one Opus, max-effort pass that groups confirmed findings into architectural patterns, cross-references `.claude/semantic-model/` and specs, and proposes whole-system structural fixes ranked by risk — not a flat bug list.

Best model/effort is concentrated on the two single-call steps (merge, synthesis) where it's cheap and highest-leverage; the multiplied steps (scan ×12, verify ×N) stay on the default model to control cost. I'll report back with the findings once it completes.

2. **The dead-abstraction pattern is measurable and bounded.** 7 of the workspace's 20 public traits have ≤1 implementation and zero polymorphic use; the other 13 are genuinely polymorphic (`CommandRunner`: 57 impls; `Manifest`: 99 use sites). This is not a "traits are overused here" culture problem — it is a specific, enumerable set of 7 traits plus 3 non-trait equivalents, all deletable.

## 2. Pattern B — No shared manifest *reader*; ecosystem dispatch re-hand-rolled

**Priority 1.** 6 instances, one of them a live panic on the release critical path.

### Instances

| Site | What it re-derives |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:277-308` | package version from a git blob (`manifest_version_at`) — **panics**; no Cargo workspace-inheritance, no Flit fallback |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:74-146` | package *name* from all three manifests — missing Flit's `tool.flit.metadata.module`, so Flit packages are silently undiscovered |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/locator.rs:104-208` | "which ecosystem is this project" — three semantics in one crate pair (multi-push in `projects()`, first-match in `declared_edges()`, membership-filtered in `IgnoreWalkLocator`) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:34-114` & `:511-582` | workspace-membership tables per ecosystem (also Pattern H) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs:15-57` vs `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:86-139` | `napi.targets` — silently-drop vs. hard-error, divergence documented and left in place |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:22-30`, `:193-200`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:652-666` | `Package` → `ReleasePackageId` via `canonical_manifests()` (×3) |

### Root cause

The canonical knowledge already exists and is correct — it just isn't *reachable* from where these callers stand:

- `ManifestFormat` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:123-210`) already owns `file_name()`, `from_path()`, `ecosystem()`. **But there is no `ManifestFormat::ALL`**, so no caller can loop over ecosystems — everyone writes `if root.join("Cargo.toml").exists() { … } else if …`. Six `src/` files independently branch on all three manifest filenames.
- `callisto-manifests` readers are **path-and-`OpenContext`-only**: `CargoToml::open(decl, ctx)`, `PackageJson::open`, `PyprojectToml::open`. A caller holding a *string* (a `git show` blob, a walker's pre-read buffer) has no supported way in, so it re-parses by hand — and hand-parsing is where the panicking `[]` indexing and the missing fallbacks come from.

### Structural fix

1. **Add the enumeration.** `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL: [ManifestFormat; N]` + `Ecosystem::canonical_formats()`. Rewrite `ignore_walk.rs`, `locator.rs` (moon), `membership.rs`, `matrix.rs`, `napi.rs` to iterate the array instead of writing three `.exists()` checks. A new ecosystem then lights up all discovery paths at once, which is the current unstated (and unmet) expectation.
2. **Add a source-level read seam to `callisto-manifests`.** Either per-type `from_source(path: &Path, source: &str, ctx: &OpenContext) -> Result<Self, ManifestError>` (with `open` becoming `read_to_string` + `from_source`), or a free function:
   ```rust
   pub fn read_identity(format: ManifestFormat, source: &str) -> Result<ManifestIdentity, ManifestError>
   // { name: Option<String>, version: Option<VersionSource> }  // VersionSource::{Literal, InheritedFromWorkspace}
   ```
   `manifest_version_at` becomes a `git show` + one call. The Cargo-workspace-inheritance case stops being an unhandled `None` and becomes an explicit `VersionSource::InheritedFromWorkspace`, which the release verifier can resolve by reading the *workspace root* blob — a decision it currently cannot even represent.
3. **Give `napi.targets` one reader** in the manifests crate returning `Result<Vec<String>, ManifestError>`; `NapiTargetsIndex::load` chooses to `.ok()` it, `matrix` chooses to propagate. One parser, two policies, policy visible at the call site.
4. **One `ReleasePackageId` derivation:** `impl Package { fn release_ids(&self) -> Result<Vec<ReleasePackageId>, …> }`; the `release.rs` variant becomes `release_ids().filter(|id| decision.entries.contains_key(id))`.

### Enforcement (makes recurrence mechanical to catch)

Add an architecture test (`crates/callisto-graph/tests/architecture.rs` or a `just arch-check` recipe) asserting that outside `callisto-model` and `callisto-manifests`, no `src/` file contains the literals `"Cargo.toml" | "package.json" | "pyproject.toml"` or a `toml_edit::DocumentMut`/`serde_json::from_str` parse of manifest content. That single grep-shaped test would have blocked all six instances. Today the count is 6 source files; the test can start with an explicit allowlist and shrink it.

**Cost:** M (a day or two; `from_source` touches three readers plus their tests). **Risk of leaving it:** high — one live panic, one silent discovery gap.

## 3. Pattern C — Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline

**Priority 2.** 3 instances. The *newer* path is the live one and it is the *less* capable one.

### Instances

| New (live) | Old (richer, effectively dead) | What the live path lost |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:287-394` (`dispatch_registry`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:172-283, 347-457, 477-528` | cargo: no `--locked`, no on-disk-version-vs-plan check; npm: **no pnpm/yarn/bun detection — plain `npm publish` in every workspace**; pypi: temp-dir build + upload-everything vs. `dist/` + normalized-name glob |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:424-469` (`dispatch_tag`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:437-465` (`GitAccess::create_tag`) | no `--` argv separator before the tag name (the old one has it, with a comment saying why); conversely the old one lacks `--no-sign` |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:87-103` | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/plan_publish.rs:12-25` | nothing — identical pipeline, one has a banner and a deprecation `eprintln!` |

Verified: `PublishOrchestrator`/`SubprocessRegistryClient` are constructed **only** inside `publish.rs`'s own `mod tests`. So this is not "two live paths drifting" — it is "the live path was rewritten from scratch against a tested reference implementation and silently dropped four behaviors." The pnpm one is a real breakage today for any pnpm/yarn workspace, and this repo's own discovery code supports `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

### Root cause

The durable-release rewrite (SPEC-RELEASE-\*) introduced a new execution model (permits, prepared effects, idempotent dispatch) and, because the old code was entangled with the old *orchestration*, reimplemented the *command construction* along with it. Command construction is the part with no orchestration content at all — it is a pure function from (ecosystem, plan, options) to an argv.

### Structural fix

1. **Extract an argv layer.** One module, e.g. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`:
   ```rust
   pub struct Argv { pub program: String, pub args: Vec<String>, pub cwd: PathBuf }
   pub fn publish_argv(target: &PublishTarget, pkg: &PlannedPackage, ws: &WorkspaceFacts) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError>;
   pub fn tag_argv(name: &TagName, target: &CommitSha, annotation: &str) -> Argv;
   ```
   Pure, no `CommandRunner`, snapshot-testable — `insta`-style assertions on exact argv per (ecosystem × package manager × registry) combination. Both `dispatch_registry` and any surviving orchestrator call it. The pnpm/yarn/bun detection and `--locked` come back for free because the snapshot tests encode them.
2. **`dispatch_tag` calls `GitAccess::create_tag`**, extended with a `sign: bool`/`TagSignPolicy` parameter so `--no-sign` and `--` coexist. `release.rs` already imports `callisto_vcs::GitAccess` (line 17, used at line 140) — the reuse path is one import away.
3. **Decide the fate of `PublishOrchestrator` explicitly.** Either delete it and its 20 tests (they currently test a code path no user reaches — a false confidence signal), or make `callisto publish` the thin deprecated alias of `plan-publish` it already is (`publish::handle` → `plan_publish::handle` + banner) and keep the orchestrator only if it is going to be promoted.

### Enforcement

Arch test: the string literals `"cargo"`, `"npm"`, `"pnpm"`, `"yarn"`, `"bun"`, `"twine"`, `"git"` may appear as a subprocess *program name* only inside the argv module and `callisto-vcs`. Grep-shaped, cheap, and it is exactly the boundary that was crossed.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — silently wrong publish tool on pnpm/yarn workspaces is a production failure, not a maintenance hazard.

## 4. Pattern D — Group severity algebra has no owning type

**Priority 3.** This is the pattern that already caused the incident that triggered this audit.

### Instances

- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:362-502` — `union_fixed` / `union_linked`, **with** a stale-member guard (skip + `UnknownPackage` diagnostic, comment naming the `MissingField` crash it prevents)
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:303-405` — inline Linked block (304-363) and Fixed block (365-405), **without** that guard; the Linked block's per-member `bump_target(id, max_sev, &input)` reaches `input.base.get(id).ok_or(MissingField)` at `cascade.rs:417-419`
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:97-140` — `fixed_group_target` recomputes the same max-severity loop a third time, called *by* `cascade.rs` after `cascade.rs` has already computed `max_sev` itself
- (secondary) `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:70-125, 127-222` — fixed/linked arms duplicated in `validate_syntactic` and `resolve` (also Pattern H)

### Root cause

"Max severity across a group, propagated back to members" is a property of `GroupTable`, but it lives as a procedure inside whichever *phase* needs it (aggregate-time, cascade-convergence-time, target-resolution-time). Each phase re-derives it because `GroupTable` exposes only `members()` — an iterator — rather than the operation. The safety guard that one phase learned (skip members absent from `base_versions`) could not propagate to the others because there was nothing shared to attach it to.

### Structural fix

Move the algebra onto the type that owns the data:

```rust
impl GroupTable {
    /// Single definition of fixed/linked severity union, including the
    /// stale-member policy. Returns per-member targets plus diagnostics.
    pub fn union_severity(
        &self,
        kind: GroupKind,
        base: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Version>,
        severities: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>,
    ) -> (BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>, Vec<Diagnostic>);
}
```

`aggregate.rs` calls it once pre-cascade; `cascade.rs`'s two blocks call it inside the convergence loop; `fixed_group_target` is deleted (its caller already has `max_sev`). The stale-member guard now exists once, so the `MissingField` crash class disappears for Linked groups as well as Fixed.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `GroupDef::members()` may be called only from `groups.rs`. That is the structural statement "group semantics live in one module," and it is checkable. Add a property test asserting `aggregate → cascade` is idempotent for a workspace containing a group member that is absent from `base_versions` — the exact shape that crashes today.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — reachable crash plus demonstrated incident history.

## 5. Pattern G — Primitives exported, compositions not

**Priority 4. Best effort-to-value ratio in the report — hours, not days.**

### Instances

1. **Credential redaction, 5 copies** of the identical one-liner `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`:
   `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs:18-20`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs:18-26`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:480-491`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:645-653`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:46-54`.
   **Supporting evidence:** `callisto-moon` has *zero* redaction call sites (`rg redact crates/callisto-moon` → no hits) while constructing `CommandOutput`/`CommandError` from raw subprocess stderr (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs:30`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner_pdk.rs:91`). The sixth crate simply never wrote the copy — which is what "composition by convention" produces.
2. **Glob compile-and-filter, 3 copies:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs:257-276` (inline), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:319-326` (`compile_glob`, not called by its own crate-sibling), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:41-56` (kept in sync *by comment*).
3. **Diagnostic line format:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs:132-142` re-inlines `render_diagnostics`' body (`:11-19`) that five sibling renderers call.

### Root cause

`callisto-model` exports `redact_known_secrets` and `known_credential_env_values` as *ingredients*. The recipe — "and the secrets come from the process environment" — is one line, so every crate writes it rather than importing it, and the one-line convention is invisible to a crate that never learns it exists. Same for `Glob::new → compile_matcher → map_err(InvalidGlob) → filter`.

### Structural fix — put the composition on the type that carries the data

```rust
// callisto-model/src/exec.rs
impl CommandOutput {
    /// stderr with known credential values redacted. Prefer over `.stderr`
    /// anywhere the text can reach a user-facing error or log.
    pub fn redacted_stderr(&self) -> String { … }
}
```
Then make the safe path the *shortest* path: make `CommandOutput.stderr` a private field with `raw_stderr()` (loud name) and `redacted_stderr()` accessors. The five locals delete themselves; `callisto-moon` gets redaction it never had; a new crate cannot forget.

Optional hardening: redact inside `CommandError::Failed`'s constructor so an unredacted stderr cannot reach an error variant at all.

Glob: one `TagGlob::compile(pattern) -> Result<TagMatcher, VcsError>` in `callisto-vcs`, re-exported; `callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` imports it and deletes its comment-enforced copy. `render_validate` calls `render_diagnostics`.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `known_credential_env_values` may be referenced only in `callisto-model`. Field privacy handles the rest via the compiler.

**Cost:** S. **Risk of leaving it:** medium-high — it is a credential-leak surface maintained by copy-paste, with one crate already missing the copy.

3. **Policy note in `AGENTS.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** at 0.x, deleting an unused `pub` item is a `patch`-with-note, not a blocker; `cargo semver-checks` failures for removals of items with zero in-repo and zero known external callers are expected and approved by the same rule.

**Cost:** S. **Risk of leaving it:** low in behavior, real in comprehension — 7 of 20 public traits being decorative teaches every future reader (and agent) that adding a trait is free.

## 7. Pattern E — Derive-twice instead of pass-the-value

**Priority 6.** Structurally identical to the incident that triggered this audit: a value is computed correctly in one place and then *re-derived* somewhere else instead of being threaded through.

### Instances

| Site | Re-derived instead of reused |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:51-74` vs `:117-141` | Floating-major tag name: template lookup → version extract → grammar resolve → parse → render → `contains_tag`, written out fully in the dry-run branch and again in the write branch. The module's doc comment says the permit split exists so "the preview branch and the write branch cannot disagree" — the split guarantees only that *a write* doesn't happen, not that the previewed *name* matches. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:13-25` | `report.packages.iter().any(|p| !p.pending_changesets.is_empty())` recomputed for the `--check` exit code, while `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:105` already computed and stored it as `StatusReport.has_changesets`. JSON output and exit code can disagree. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:23-66` | `--staged` and `--since` each run their own git diff, error-map, quote-strip, and `ends_with` filter; only the argv differs. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:87-103` vs `plan_publish.rs:12-25` | (also Pattern C) same plan-and-render pipeline wired twice |

### Structural fix — plan-then-execute, mechanically

1. `tag.rs`: one pure `fn plan_floating_major(ws, release) -> Result<Option<FloatingMajorPlan>, GraphError>` returning `{ name: TagName, already_existed: bool }`. Preview renders the plan; the write branch consumes the *same* value it was handed. The permit then gates only `git.create_floating_major(plan.name)`.
2. `status.rs`: `check_exit_code_raw` reads `report.has_changesets`. One-line fix; the general rule is *the CLI never recomputes a field the report already carries* — enforceable as a review checklist item and partially by making derived report fields the only public accessor.
3. `validate.rs`: `fn changed_files(runner, root, args: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<String>, GraphError>`; both branches supply argv only.
4. **The general rule worth writing into `AGENTS.md`:** any `if permit.is_some()` / `if dry_run` split must branch on *executing a plan value*, never on *recomputing the plan*. That single sentence describes both this pattern and the original incident.

**Cost:** M (mostly mechanical). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — no live bug found, but this is the incident's exact shape and the release path already has two variants of it (`tag.rs`, and Pattern C's preview command).

## 8. Pattern F — Raw `String` identifiers, so validation lives at call sites

**Priority 7.** Security-adjacent, medium cost.

### Instances

- **GitHub owner/repo, three notions, two validators, one crate:**
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:1009-1014` `is_safe_github_repository` — no character class at all; `"owner name/repo"` passes. Used at `release.rs:923` in `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::new` — the artifact-attestation provenance boundary.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs:394-411` `validate_repository`/`valid_repo_part` — ASCII alnum + `-_.` per part.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:1201` — a **third** construction, `format!("{owner}/{repository}")` from a parsed remote URL with no validation, feeding `dispatch_forge_release`.
  - The field is declared as bare `repository: String` in ~6 struct/constructor positions across `release.rs` and `release_pr.rs`.
- **`TagName(pub String)`** (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs:163-172`) — unvalidated newtype with a *public* field, so a tag name that looks like a flag is constructible. That is why the missing `--` separator in `dispatch_tag` (Pattern C) is more than cosmetic: the `--` is currently the *only* defense, and the live path doesn't have it.
- (context) `GroupName`/`RegistryKey` are documented in `.claude/semantic-model/core-identity.md` as "String newtypes with no validation beyond non-emptiness" — same shape, lower stakes.

### Structural fix — parse, don't validate

```rust
// callisto-model
pub struct GitHubRepository { owner: String, repo: String }   // private fields
impl GitHubRepository {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, InvalidGitHubRepository>; // one charset, one rule
    pub fn as_slug(&self) -> String;   // "owner/repo"
}
```
Replace every `repository: String` in `release.rs`/`release_pr.rs` with `GitHubRepository`; delete both validators; make `release.rs:1201` construct via `parse`. Do the same for `TagName`: private field + `TagName::parse` rejecting leading `-`, control chars, and git's `check-ref-format` illegal sequences. Then the argv `--` becomes defense-in-depth rather than the sole guard.

**Enforcement:** the type system — an unvalidated slug becomes unconstructible.
