489	    "synthesis": "# Duplicate Logic & Over-Engineering: Pattern Report

**Workspace:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto` (10 crates, ~55.5k LOC of `src/`)
**Input:** 32 verified findings
**Method:** findings regrouped by *root cause*, then verified against source; two claims were escalated with new evidence (see §New Evidence).

---

## 0. Executive Summary

The 32 findings collapse into **8 architectural patterns**. Three of them (B, C, D) sit directly on the release/publish critical path — the same path whose duplicate-derivation bug just broke every release in a fixed-group workspace. One (G) is security-sensitive. One (A) is 10 findings' worth of pure deletion at near-zero risk.

Two headline results from re-verification:

1. **`manifest_version_at` does not fail closed — it panics.** The hand-rolled manifest parser in the release-commit verifier uses `toml_edit`'s panicking `Index` impl (`document["project"]["version"]`) where the canonical reader it duplicates uses safe `.get()` chains. Empirically confirmed against toml_edit 0.22.27: a Poetry-only `pyproject.toml`, a PEP 621 `dynamic = ["version"]` project, or any `Cargo.toml` without `[package]` panics with `index not found` inside `derive_release_commit_decision`. This upgrades finding #4 from "fails closed" to "aborts the release verifier". Details in §New Evidence.
2. **The dead-abstraction pattern is measurable and bounded.** 7 of the workspace's 20 public traits have ≤1 implementation and zero polymorphic use; the other 13 are genuinely polymorphic (`CommandRunner`: 57 impls; `Manifest`: 99 use sites). This is not a "traits are overused here" culture problem — it is a specific, enumerable set of 7 traits plus 3 non-trait equivalents, all deletable.

---

## 1. Pattern Index

| # | Pattern | Findings | On release/publish path | Fix cost | Risk if left | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B** | No shared *reader* for "what does this manifest say" — ecosystem dispatch re-hand-rolled per call site | 6 | **Yes (crash)** | M | **High** | **1** |
| **C** | Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline coexist; the live one re-typed the dead one's commands and lost capability | 3 | **Yes** | M | **High** | **2** |
| **D** | Fixed/linked group severity algebra has no owning type | 2 (+1) | **Yes (prior incident)** | M | **High** | **3** |
| **G** | Shared *primitives* are exported; shared *compositions* are not | 3 (5+3+1 copies) | Partly (publish stderr) | **S** | Med-High (security) | **4** |
| **A** | Speculative seams: abstraction built for a second consumer that never arrived | 10 | No | **S** | Low (comprehension tax) | **5** |
| **E** | Derive-twice instead of pass-the-value (preview vs. apply, CLI vs. report) | 4 | Partly | M | Med (this is the incident's shape) | **6** |
| **F** | Domain identifiers are raw `String`, so validation is a call-site concern and diverges | 2 (+1) | Yes (attestation, tags) | M | Med | **7** |
| **H** | Parallel arms hand-written over a closed set of kinds | 6 | No | **L** | Low-Med | **8** |

Findings map 1:1 onto patterns; a few carry a secondary pattern, noted inline.

---

## 2. Pattern B — No shared manifest *reader*; ecosystem dispatch re-hand-rolled

**Priority 1.** 6 instances, one of them a live panic on the release critical path.

### Instances

| Site | What it re-derives |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:277-308` | package version from a git blob (`manifest_version_at`) — **panics**; no Cargo workspace-inheritance, no Flit fallback |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:74-146` | package *name* from all three manifests — missing Flit's `tool.flit.metadata.module`, so Flit packages are silently undiscovered |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/locator.rs:104-208` | "which ecosystem is this project" — three semantics in one crate pair (multi-push in `projects()`, first-match in `declared_edges()`, membership-filtered in `IgnoreWalkLocator`) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:34-114` & `:511-582` | workspace-membership tables per ecosystem (also Pattern H) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs:15-57` vs `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:86-139` | `napi.targets` — silently-drop vs. hard-error, divergence documented and left in place |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:22-30`, `:193-200`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:652-666` | `Package` → `ReleasePackageId` via `canonical_manifests()` (×3) |

### Root cause

The canonical knowledge already exists and is correct — it just isn't *reachable* from where these callers stand:

- `ManifestFormat` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:123-210`) already owns `file_name()`, `from_path()`, `ecosystem()`. **But there is no `ManifestFormat::ALL`**, so no caller can loop over ecosystems — everyone writes `if root.join("Cargo.toml").exists() { … } else if …`. Six `src/` files independently branch on all three manifest filenames.
- `callisto-manifests` readers are **path-and-`OpenContext`-only**: `CargoToml::open(decl, ctx)`, `PackageJson::open`, `PyprojectToml::open`. A caller holding a *string* (a `git show` blob, a walker's pre-read buffer) has no supported way in, so it re-parses by hand — and hand-parsing is where the panicking `[]` indexing and the missing fallbacks come from.

### Structural fix

1. **Add the enumeration.** `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL: [ManifestFormat; N]` + `Ecosystem::canonical_formats()`. Rewrite `ignore_walk.rs`, `locator.rs` (moon), `membership.rs`, `matrix.rs`, `napi.rs` to iterate the array instead of writing three `.exists()` checks. A new ecosystem then lights up all discovery paths at once, which is the current unstated (and unmet) expectation.
2. **Add a source-level read seam to `callisto-manifests`.** Either per-type `from_source(path: &Path, source: &str, ctx: &OpenContext) -> Result<Self, ManifestError>` (with `open` becoming `read_to_string` + `from_source`), or a free function:
   ```rust
   pub fn read_identity(format: ManifestFormat, source: &str) -> Result<ManifestIdentity, ManifestError>
   // { name: Option<String>, version: Option<VersionSource> }  // VersionSource::{Literal, InheritedFromWorkspace}
   ```
   `manifest_version_at` becomes a `git show` + one call. The Cargo-workspace-inheritance case stops being an unhandled `None` and becomes an explicit `VersionSource::InheritedFromWorkspace`, which the release verifier can resolve by reading the *workspace root* blob — a decision it currently cannot even represent.
3. **Give `napi.targets` one reader** in the manifests crate returning `Result<Vec<String>, ManifestError>`; `NapiTargetsIndex::load` chooses to `.ok()` it, `matrix` chooses to propagate. One parser, two policies, policy visible at the call site.
4. **One `ReleasePackageId` derivation:** `impl Package { fn release_ids(&self) -> Result<Vec<ReleasePackageId>, …> }`; the `release.rs` variant becomes `release_ids().filter(|id| decision.entries.contains_key(id))`.

### Enforcement (makes recurrence mechanical to catch)

Add an architecture test (`crates/callisto-graph/tests/architecture.rs` or a `just arch-check` recipe) asserting that outside `callisto-model` and `callisto-manifests`, no `src/` file contains the literals `"Cargo.toml" | "package.json" | "pyproject.toml"` or a `toml_edit::DocumentMut`/`serde_json::from_str` parse of manifest content. That single grep-shaped test would have blocked all six instances. Today the count is 6 source files; the test can start with an explicit allowlist and shrink it.

**Cost:** M (a day or two; `from_source` touches three readers plus their tests). **Risk of leaving it:** high — one live panic, one silent discovery gap.

---

## 3. Pattern C — Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline

**Priority 2.** 3 instances. The *newer* path is the live one and it is the *less* capable one.

### Instances

| New (live) | Old (richer, effectively dead) | What the live path lost |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:287-394` (`dispatch_registry`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:172-283, 347-457, 477-528` | cargo: no `--locked`, no on-disk-version-vs-plan check; npm: **no pnpm/yarn/bun detection — plain `npm publish` in every workspace**; pypi: temp-dir build + upload-everything vs. `dist/` + normalized-name glob |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:424-469` (`dispatch_tag`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:437-465` (`GitAccess::create_tag`) | no `--` argv separator before the tag name (the old one has it, with a comment saying why); conversely the old one lacks `--no-sign` |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:87-103` | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/plan_publish.rs:12-25` | nothing — identical pipeline, one has a banner and a deprecation `eprintln!` |

Verified: `PublishOrchestrator`/`SubprocessRegistryClient` are constructed **only** inside `publish.rs`'s own `mod tests`. So this is not "two live paths drifting" — it is "the live path was rewritten from scratch against a tested reference implementation and silently dropped four behaviors." The pnpm one is a real breakage today for any pnpm/yarn workspace, and this repo's own discovery code supports `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

### Root cause

The durable-release rewrite (SPEC-RELEASE-\*) introduced a new execution model (permits, prepared effects, idempotent dispatch) and, because the old code was entangled with the old *orchestration*, reimplemented the *command construction* along with it. Command construction is the part with no orchestration content at all — it is a pure function from (ecosystem, plan, options) to an argv.

### Structural fix

1. **Extract an argv layer.** One module, e.g. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`:
   ```rust
   pub struct Argv { pub program: String, pub args: Vec<String>, pub cwd: PathBuf }
   pub fn publish_argv(target: &PublishTarget, pkg: &PlannedPackage, ws: &WorkspaceFacts) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError>;
   pub fn tag_argv(name: &TagName, target: &CommitSha, annotation: &str) -> Argv;
   ```
   Pure, no `CommandRunner`, snapshot-testable — `insta`-style assertions on exact argv per (ecosystem × package manager × registry) combination. Both `dispatch_registry` and any surviving orchestrator call it. The pnpm/yarn/bun detection and `--locked` come back for free because the snapshot tests encode them.
2. **`dispatch_tag` calls `GitAccess::create_tag`**, extended with a `sign: bool`/`TagSignPolicy` parameter so `--no-sign` and `--` coexist. `release.rs` already imports `callisto_vcs::GitAccess` (line 17, used at line 140) — the reuse path is one import away.
3. **Decide the fate of `PublishOrchestrator` explicitly.** Either delete it and its 20 tests (they currently test a code path no user reaches — a false confidence signal), or make `callisto publish` the thin deprecated alias of `plan-publish` it already is (`publish::handle` → `plan_publish::handle` + banner) and keep the orchestrator only if it is going to be promoted.

### Enforcement

Arch test: the string literals `"cargo"`, `"npm"`, `"pnpm"`, `"yarn"`, `"bun"`, `"twine"`, `"git"` may appear as a subprocess *program name* only inside the argv module and `callisto-vcs`. Grep-shaped, cheap, and it is exactly the boundary that was crossed.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — silently wrong publish tool on pnpm/yarn workspaces is a production failure, not a maintenance hazard.

---

## 4. Pattern D — Group severity algebra has no owning type

**Priority 3.** This is the pattern that already caused the incident that triggered this audit.

### Instances

- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:362-502` — `union_fixed` / `union_linked`, **with** a stale-member guard (skip + `UnknownPackage` diagnostic, comment naming the `MissingField` crash it prevents)
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:303-405` — inline Linked block (304-363) and Fixed block (365-405), **without** that guard; the Linked block's per-member `bump_target(id, max_sev, &input)` reaches `input.base.get(id).ok_or(MissingField)` at `cascade.rs:417-419`
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:97-140` — `fixed_group_target` recomputes the same max-severity loop a third time, called *by* `cascade.rs` after `cascade.rs` has already computed `max_sev` itself
- (secondary) `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:70-125, 127-222` — fixed/linked arms duplicated in `validate_syntactic` and `resolve` (also Pattern H)

### Root cause

"Max severity across a group, propagated back to members" is a property of `GroupTable`, but it lives as a procedure inside whichever *phase* needs it (aggregate-time, cascade-convergence-time, target-resolution-time). Each phase re-derives it because `GroupTable` exposes only `members()` — an iterator — rather than the operation. The safety guard that one phase learned (skip members absent from `base_versions`) could not propagate to the others because there was nothing shared to attach it to.

### Structural fix

Move the algebra onto the type that owns the data:

```rust
impl GroupTable {
    /// Single definition of fixed/linked severity union, including the
    /// stale-member policy. Returns per-member targets plus diagnostics.
    pub fn union_severity(
        &self,
        kind: GroupKind,
        base: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Version>,
        severities: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>,
    ) -> (BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>, Vec<Diagnostic>);
}
```

`aggregate.rs` calls it once pre-cascade; `cascade.rs`'s two blocks call it inside the convergence loop; `fixed_group_target` is deleted (its caller already has `max_sev`). The stale-member guard now exists once, so the `MissingField` crash class disappears for Linked groups as well as Fixed.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `GroupDef::members()` may be called only from `groups.rs`. That is the structural statement "group semantics live in one module," and it is checkable. Add a property test asserting `aggregate → cascade` is idempotent for a workspace containing a group member that is absent from `base_versions` — the exact shape that crashes today.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — reachable crash plus demonstrated incident history.

---

## 5. Pattern G — Primitives exported, compositions not

**Priority 4. Best effort-to-value ratio in the report — hours, not days.**

### Instances

1. **Credential redaction, 5 copies** of the identical one-liner `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`:
   `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs:18-20`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs:18-26`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:480-491`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:645-653`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:46-54`.
   **Supporting evidence:** `callisto-moon` has *zero* redaction call sites (`rg redact crates/callisto-moon` → no hits) while constructing `CommandOutput`/`CommandError` from raw subprocess stderr (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs:30`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner_pdk.rs:91`). The sixth crate simply never wrote the copy — which is what "composition by convention" produces.
2. **Glob compile-and-filter, 3 copies:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs:257-276` (inline), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:319-326` (`compile_glob`, not called by its own crate-sibling), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:41-56` (kept in sync *by comment*).
3. **Diagnostic line format:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs:132-142` re-inlines `render_diagnostics`' body (`:11-19`) that five sibling renderers call.

### Root cause

`callisto-model` exports `redact_known_secrets` and `known_credential_env_values` as *ingredients*. The recipe — "and the secrets come from the process environment" — is one line, so every crate writes it rather than importing it, and the one-line convention is invisible to a crate that never learns it exists. Same for `Glob::new → compile_matcher → map_err(InvalidGlob) → filter`.

### Structural fix — put the composition on the type that carries the data

```rust
// callisto-model/src/exec.rs
impl CommandOutput {
    /// stderr with known credential values redacted. Prefer over `.stderr`
    /// anywhere the text can reach a user-facing error or log.
    pub fn redacted_stderr(&self) -> String { … }
}
```
Then make the safe path the *shortest* path: make `CommandOutput.stderr` a private field with `raw_stderr()` (loud name) and `redacted_stderr()` accessors. The five locals delete themselves; `callisto-moon` gets redaction it never had; a new crate cannot forget.

Optional hardening: redact inside `CommandError::Failed`'s constructor so an unredacted stderr cannot reach an error variant at all.

Glob: one `TagGlob::compile(pattern) -> Result<TagMatcher, VcsError>` in `callisto-vcs`, re-exported; `callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` imports it and deletes its comment-enforced copy. `render_validate` calls `render_diagnostics`.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `known_credential_env_values` may be referenced only in `callisto-model`. Field privacy handles the rest via the compiler.

**Cost:** S. **Risk of leaving it:** medium-high — it is a credential-leak surface maintained by copy-paste, with one crate already missing the copy.

---

## 6. Pattern A — Speculative seams

**Priority 5.** Largest instance count (10), lowest risk, essentially pure deletion.

### Trait census (whole workspace, measured)

| Trait | impls | `dyn`/generic uses | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CommandRunner` | 57 | 126 | healthy |
| `Manifest` | 3 | 99 | healthy |
| `DependencyResolver` | 9 | 65 | healthy |
| `SeverityInference` | 9 | 19 | healthy |
| `Report`, `CommitWalker`, `RegistryClient`, `GitDataSource`, `ProjectLocator`, `Versioning`, `RateLimitPolicy`, `TimeProvider`, `ReleaseStateWriter` | 2-10 | 3-14 | healthy |
| **`CascadeSolver`** | **0** | **0** | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:155-165`) |
| **`GitVcsProvider`** | 1 | 1 (its own impl) | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs:71-75`) — `GitDataSource` supersedes it |
| **`PackageIdentityResolver`** | 1 | 1 | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:163-173`) |
| **`ChangesetStorage`** | 1 | 2 (re-exports) | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs:15-29` + 2 re-exports in `callisto-manifests`) |
| **`ReleaseEffectAdapter`** | 1 | 3 | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs:26-49`) |
| **`ManifestCstEditor`** | 1 (blanket) | 0 | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:62-90`) — actively *counter*-productive: it fuses write+persist, defeating the write-batching that `apply.rs` deliberately does |
| **`ReportPresenter`** | 1 (test-only `FakeReport`) | 1 | delete (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs:37-44`) |

Non-trait instances of the same disease:

- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs:116-145` — `RawMoonYml`/`RawMoonExtensions`/`RawMoonCallistoConfig`: a full config schema nothing deserializes; also the only `Raw*` structs in the file missing `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, corroborating "never wired up."
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:47-91` + `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:215-221` — `check_credentials` is `#[cfg(test)]` (absent from the binary) with 5 tests; `skip_publish_precheck` is parsed into `let _skip_publish_precheck = …`. A mechanism with a knob, neither reachable — and the flag's help text describes a *different* feature than the dead code.
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:84-91, 118-135` — `last_tag_for` + `select_from_tags`, documented as "kept for API compatibility with existing callers," called only by their own tests; `TagIndex::build` uses `select_from_tags_cached`.

### Root cause

Nothing in the repo distinguishes *a designed extension point* from *an abstraction added reflexively at write time*, and `just check-api` (`cargo semver-checks check-release`) makes removing a `pub` item feel like a breaking-change event. So dead API accretes and is then defended by tests written to exercise the dead API — which is why several of these look "covered."

### Structural fix

1. **Delete all 10.** Zero behavioral risk: each is either a one-line forward or has no caller. `ManifestCstEditor`'s removal deletes two tests that test only the trait.
2. **Write the rule down and enforce it.** Add `crates/*/tests/` or `just arch-check`: every `pub trait` must have ≥2 `impl` blocks **or** at least one `dyn Trait` / `T: Trait` use site, otherwise fail — unless listed in `arch-allow.toml` with a one-line reason and an owner. The census above shows the check is cleanly separable today (healthy traits score 3-126; dead ones score 0-3), so it will not produce noise.
3. **Policy note in `AGENTS.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** at 0.x, deleting an unused `pub` item is a `patch`-with-note, not a blocker; `cargo semver-checks` failures for removals of items with zero in-repo and zero known external callers are expected and approved by the same rule.

**Cost:** S. **Risk of leaving it:** low in behavior, real in comprehension — 7 of 20 public traits being decorative teaches every future reader (and agent) that adding a trait is free.

## 7. Pattern E — Derive-twice instead of pass-the-value

**Priority 6.** Structurally identical to the incident that triggered this audit: a value is computed correctly in one place and then *re-derived* somewhere else instead of being threaded through.

### Instances

| Site | Re-derived instead of reused |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:51-74` vs `:117-141` | Floating-major tag name: template lookup → version extract → grammar resolve → parse → render → `contains_tag`, written out fully in the dry-run branch and again in the write branch. The module's doc comment says the permit split exists so "the preview branch and the write branch cannot disagree" — the split guarantees only that *a write* doesn't happen, not that the previewed *name* matches. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:13-25` | `report.packages.iter().any(|p| !p.pending_changesets.is_empty())` recomputed for the `--check` exit code, while `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:105` already computed and stored it as `StatusReport.has_changesets`. JSON output and exit code can disagree. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:23-66` | `--staged` and `--since` each run their own git diff, error-map, quote-strip, and `ends_with` filter; only the argv differs. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:87-103` vs `plan_publish.rs:12-25` | (also Pattern C) same plan-and-render pipeline wired twice |

### Structural fix — plan-then-execute, mechanically

1. `tag.rs`: one pure `fn plan_floating_major(ws, release) -> Result<Option<FloatingMajorPlan>, GraphError>` returning `{ name: TagName, already_existed: bool }`. Preview renders the plan; the write branch consumes the *same* value it was handed. The permit then gates only `git.create_floating_major(plan.name)`.
2. `status.rs`: `check_exit_code_raw` reads `report.has_changesets`. One-line fix; the general rule is *the CLI never recomputes a field the report already carries* — enforceable as a review checklist item and partially by making derived report fields the only public accessor.
3. `validate.rs`: `fn changed_files(runner, root, args: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<String>, GraphError>`; both branches supply argv only.
4. **The general rule worth writing into `AGENTS.md`:** any `if permit.is_some()` / `if dry_run` split must branch on *executing a plan value*, never on *recomputing the plan*. That single sentence describes both this pattern and the original incident.

**Cost:** M (mostly mechanical). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — no live bug found, but this is the incident's exact shape and the release path already has two variants of it (`tag.rs`, and Pattern C's preview command).

---

## 8. Pattern F — Raw `String` identifiers, so validation lives at call sites

**Priority 7.** Security-adjacent, medium cost.

### Instances

- **GitHub owner/repo, three notions, two validators, one crate:**
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:1009-1014` `is_safe_github_repository` — no character class at all; `"owner name/repo"` passes. Used at `release.rs:923` in `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::new` — the artifact-attestation provenance boundary.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs:394-411` `validate_repository`/`valid_repo_part` — ASCII alnum + `-_.` per part.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:1201` — a **third** construction, `format!("{owner}/{repository}")` from a parsed remote URL with no validation, feeding `dispatch_forge_release`.
  - The field is declared as bare `repository: String` in ~6 struct/constructor positions across `release.rs` and `release_pr.rs`.
- **`TagName(pub String)`** (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs:163-172`) — unvalidated newtype with a *public* field, so a tag name that looks like a flag is constructible. That is why the missing `--` separator in `dispatch_tag` (Pattern C) is more than cosmetic: the `--` is currently the *only* defense, and the live path doesn't have it.
- (context) `GroupName`/`RegistryKey` are documented in `.claude/semantic-model/core-identity.md` as "String newtypes with no validation beyond non-emptiness" — same shape, lower stakes.

### Structural fix — parse, don't validate

```rust
// callisto-model
pub struct GitHubRepository { owner: String, repo: String }   // private fields
impl GitHubRepository {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, InvalidGitHubRepository>; // one charset, one rule
    pub fn as_slug(&self) -> String;   // "owner/repo"
}
```
Replace every `repository: String` in `release.rs`/`release_pr.rs` with `GitHubRepository`; delete both validators; make `release.rs:1201` construct via `parse`. Do the same for `TagName`: private field + `TagName::parse` rejecting leading `-`, control chars, and git's `check-ref-format` illegal sequences. Then the argv `--` becomes defense-in-depth rather than the sole guard.

**Enforcement:** the type system — an unvalidated slug becomes unconstructible.

**Cost:** M (a mechanical type substitution across ~8 fields plus serde round-trip tests). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — the looser validator guards the more security-sensitive boundary, which is the wrong way round.

---

## 9. Pattern H — Parallel arms over a closed set of kinds

**Priority 8.** Largest code volume, lowest incident probability, highest refactor risk. **Be honest: this one cannot be made structurally impossible — only cheaper.**

### Instances

| Site | Duplicated axis |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:350-485` | `[[package]]` vs `[[package-set]]` — same 5 fields, same 5 sub-parsers, same `PackageConfig` literal; differs by pattern parser + error prefix |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:70-125, 127-222` | fixed vs linked — validation and member resolution, twice |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:34-114` vs `:511-582` | Cargo vs Python membership; comment literally says "Mirrors CargoMembership exactly" |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:201-243` vs `:612-644`, `:285-377` vs `:646-708` | member manifest vs workspace root — decor-preserving TOML write, twice, incl. the three dependency shapes and the `UnrecognizedDependencyValue` fallback |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:220-243, 296-334, 404-455` | PEP 508 decomposition (marker split → first operator → extras split) written from scratch three times — read path can disagree with both write paths |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs:60-87` | three header-shape branches with identical 5-statement tails |

### Structural fix — introduce the missing *values*, not a code-sharing scheme

The reason these copies exist is that the thing varying (a group kind, a rule kind, an ecosystem's membership table, a requirement string) has no representation, so the variation is expressed as code structure.

1. **PEP 508 gets a type.** `struct Requirement { name, extras, op_and_spec, marker }` with `parse` / `render` and a round-trip property test. All three sites collapse to `Requirement::parse(s)?` and the read/write disagreement becomes unrepresentable. Natural home: `callisto-format` (Layer 1, permissive) or `callisto-manifests::common`.
2. **TOML decor gets a helper.** `fn set_preserving_decor(item: &mut Item, key: &str, value: Value)` + `fn set_dependency_version(item: &mut Item, v: &str) -> Result<(), ManifestError>` handling the three shapes once. `CargoToml` and `WorkspaceCargoResolver` both call it; the extensive decor test suite in that file then covers one implementation instead of two.
3. **Kind becomes a parameter.** `GroupTable::resolve` takes `GroupKind` and loops `[Fixed, Linked]`; `ResolvedConfig::load` gets `fn resolve_package_config(raw: &RawPackageCommon, kind_label: &str) -> Result<PackageConfig, ConfigError>` called by both loops, so a new `PackageConfig` field is a compile error in exactly one place.
4. **Membership becomes generic.** `struct Membership { members, exclude, hybrid_root }` + `fn read_membership(root, spec: &MembershipSpec)` where `MembershipSpec` names the file and the TOML path. Pairs naturally with Pattern B's `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL`.
5. `write.rs::prepend`: compute `rest` in the if/else, then one shared tail.

**Cost:** L (spread across three crates; `cargo.rs` and `python.rs` have dense test suites that must keep passing byte-for-byte). **Risk of leaving it:** low-medium; no divergence observed today in most of these. **Recommendation: do #1 and #2 (real correctness content), defer #3-#5** unless touched for another reason.

---

## 10. Priority Ranking & Suggested Sequencing

| Rank | Pattern | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **B** — manifest reader | Contains the only *live crash* (§New Evidence), plus a silent discovery gap for Flit packages. On the release verification path. Fix is additive (new constructors, new const) before it is subtractive. |
| 2 | **C** — two pipeline generations | The live publish path is missing `--locked`, the on-disk version check, and package-manager detection. A pnpm workspace publishes with the wrong tool **today**. Also the tag-injection guard is on the dead path only. |
| 3 | **D** — group algebra | Already caused a production incident in this exact area; a reachable `MissingField` crash remains for Linked groups. Bounded, three call sites. |
| 4 | **G** — compositions | Hours of work; removes a five-way-copied security control and gives `callisto-moon` redaction it currently lacks entirely. |
| 5 | **A** — dead seams | 10 instances, near-zero behavioral risk, and it is the pattern most likely to keep recurring silently. Do it as one deletion PR plus the census test. |
| 6 | **E** — derive-twice | No live bug, but structurally identical to the incident; `tag.rs` preview/write is the one worth fixing first. |
| 7 | **F** — raw String identity | Security-adjacent; the weaker validator guards the attestation boundary. Medium cost, no urgency signal. |
| 8 | **H** — parallel arms | Largest volume, smallest observed divergence, highest regression risk. Take the two with correctness content (PEP 508, TOML decor); defer the rest. |

**Suggested workstreams (not 8 sequential PRs):**

- **W1 — "Release path single source of truth" (B + C + D).** These three share reviewers, tests, and blast radius, and together they close every high-severity finding. Order inside: B's `from_source` seam → D's `GroupTable::union_severity` → C's argv extraction. Land the `manifest_version_at` panic fix *first and alone* as a hotfix.
- **W2 — "Delete the decorations" (A + G).** One deletion PR (A) + one hardening PR (G). Small, independent, safe to run in parallel with W1.
- **W3 — "Plan values and parsed identities" (E + F).** Follows W1 naturally since both touch the same modules.
- **W4 — opportunistic (H).** Only when the surrounding file is already being modified.

**Enforcement summary — the four arch tests that make five of the eight patterns non-recurring.** All are grep- or census-shaped and belong in one `just arch-check` recipe wired into `ci-fast`:

1. Manifest filename literals & raw manifest parsing confined to `callisto-model` + `callisto-manifests` (kills B).
2. Subprocess program names confined to the argv module + `callisto-vcs` (kills C).
3. `GroupDef::members()` confined to `groups.rs` (kills D).
4. Every `pub trait` has ≥2 impls or a polymorphic use, else allowlisted with a reason (kills A).
   Plus, by the type system rather than a test: private fields on `CommandOutput.stderr`, `TagName.0`, and a new `GitHubRepository` (kill G and F).

---

## 11. New Evidence (escalations beyond the 32 findings)

**E1 — `manifest_version_at` panics; it does not fail closed. (Escalates finding #4 to critical.)**

`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:286-303` uses `toml_edit`'s `Index` impl:

```rust
.and_then(|document| document["package"]["version"].as_str().map(str::to_owned)),
…
document["project"]["version"].as_str()
    .or_else(|| document["tool"]["poetry"]["version"].as_str())
```

`toml_edit` 0.22.27's `impl Index<&str> for Table` is `self.get(key).expect("index not found")` (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/toml_edit-0.22.27/src/index.rs:102-107`), and `DocumentMut`'s forwards to it. Confirmed empirically with a scratch binary against the same crate version — all three panic:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Poetry-only `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.poetry]`, no `[project]`) | `panicked at 'index not found'` |
| PEP 621 `[project]` with `dynamic = ["version"]` | `panicked at 'index not found'` |
| `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]` and no `[package]` | `panicked at 'index not found'` |

Reachability: `derive_release_commit_decision` (`release_decision.rs:207-219`) calls `manifest_version_at` **unconditionally, for every canonical manifest of every package in the graph, at both the parent and the release commit** — not just packages being released. So one Poetry-managed Python package anywhere in the workspace aborts release-commit verification with a panic instead of the intended `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale`.

Contrast with the canonical reader it duplicates, `PyprojectToml::current_version` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:135-158`), which uses safe `.get()` chains, has the Poetry *and* Flit fallbacks, and returns a typed `ManifestError::MissingField`. This is the single clearest argument for Pattern B's fix.

A survey of the whole workspace found **no other panicking manifest index** in production code: `python.rs:204` and `init.rs:82,88` are `IndexMut` (inserting, safe), and `membership.rs:273` is `yaml_rust2`, whose `Index` returns `BadValue` rather than panicking (documented at `membership.rs:265-268`).

**E2 — `callisto-moon` has no redaction at all.** `rg redact crates/callisto-moon` returns zero hits, while `runner.rs:30` and `runner_pdk.rs:91` construct `CommandOutput` from raw subprocess stderr. Not a confirmed leak (no user-facing error formatting found there yet), but it demonstrates the failure mode of Pattern G: the convention doesn't propagate to a crate that never learned it.

---

## 12. Borderline / Flag for Human Triage (do not act unilaterally)

1. **Is Pattern C duplication or dead code?** `PublishOrchestrator`/`SubprocessRegistryClient` are constructed only in tests, and `callisto publish` is documented as a dry-run compatibility preview. Deleting them removes ~20 passing tests; keeping them keeps a richer reference implementation. **Decision needed from the owner: promote or delete.** Either way, extract the argv layer first — that part is unambiguous.
2. **`--no-sign` vs `--` in tag creation (finding #6).** These may be *deliberately* different: `--no-sign` matters in CI where `commit.gpgsign` is set globally (this repo's own test-hang history involves global gpgsign). Unifying must **keep** `--no-sign` and **add** `--`, not pick one implementation. Confirm with the release owner before collapsing.
3. **Tightening `is_safe_github_repository` (finding #3)** is a behavior change on a validation boundary. GitHub's own charset matches the stricter rule, but a repo slug that currently passes and would then fail is a hard error at `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::new`. Ship with a changeset and a migration note.
4. **Removing public items is `cargo semver-checks`-visible** (`just check-api`). `ChangesetStorage`, `last_tag_for`, `GitVcsProvider`, `PackageIdentityResolver`, `ReportPresenter`, `ManifestCstEditor` are all `pub` on published 0.6 crates. Needs an explicit policy call (proposed in §6) before the deletion PR lands.
5. **`ManifestCstEditor` is named in a spec.** `.claude/specs/SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001.json`'s reasoning trail explicitly covers it in AC-014 while noting it has zero callers. Deleting it needs a spec amendment, not just a code PR.
6. **`skip_publish_precheck` is public CLI surface** (`cli.rs:215-221`), and its help text describes an "already published?" check — a *different* feature from the dead `check_credentials`. Removing the flag is a user-visible CLI break; implementing it is new work. Product decision, not a cleanup.
7. **Finding #9's crash claim is precise for Linked groups only.** The Fixed-group path routes through `fixed_group_target`, which has a soft fallback rather than the `MissingField` panic. The duplication and the guard asymmetry are real for both; the crash is demonstrated for Linked.
8. **Finding #29's `declared_edges` comparison isn't apples-to-apples.** `IgnoreWalkLocator` doesn't implement `declared_edges` at all (it takes the trait default `None`, `locate/mod.rs:14-16`), and its "Cargo-before-npm" test pins *sort order*, not exclusivity — it still returns both ecosystems. The well-supported half is `projects()`: membership filtering exists in one locator and not the other. Also a genuine product question: **should** the moon locator apply Cargo/npm/uv membership filtering, or does moon own project boundaries by design? Answer that before unifying.
9. **Finding #8 (`ReleasePackageId` ×3) is currently consistent**, and the `release.rs` variant's extra ecosystem-presence filter is intentional. Low value on its own; fold it into Pattern B's work rather than as a standalone PR.
10. **Finding #22 (`has_changesets`)** — verify no intentional difference between the JSON field and the `--check` semantics (e.g. a package category deliberately excluded from one) before switching the CLI to read the field. Very likely a one-line fix, but confirm with a test that asserts the two agree."

"synthesis": "# Duplicate Logic & Over-Engineering: Pattern Report

**Workspace:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto` (10 crates, ~55.5k LOC of `src/`)
**Input:** 32 verified findings
**Method:** findings regrouped by *root cause*, then verified against source; two claims were escalated with new evidence (see §New Evidence).

---

## 0. Executive Summary

The 32 findings collapse into **8 architectural patterns**. Three of them (B, C, D) sit directly on the release/publish critical path — the same path whose duplicate-derivation bug just broke every release in a fixed-group workspace. One (G) is security-sensitive. One (A) is 10 findings' worth of pure deletion at near-zero risk.

Two headline results from re-verification:

1. **`manifest_version_at` does not fail closed — it panics.** The hand-rolled manifest parser in the release-commit verifier uses `toml_edit`'s panicking `Index` impl (`document["project"]["version"]`) where the canonical reader it duplicates uses safe `.get()` chains. Empirically confirmed against toml_edit 0.22.27: a Poetry-only `pyproject.toml`, a PEP 621 `dynamic = ["version"]` project, or any `Cargo.toml` without `[package]` panics with `index not found` inside `derive_release_commit_decision`. This upgrades finding #4 from "fails closed" to "aborts the release verifier". Details in §New Evidence.
2. **The dead-abstraction pattern is measurable and bounded.** 7 of the workspace's 20 public traits have ≤1 implementation and zero polymorphic use; the other 13 are genuinely polymorphic (`CommandRunner`: 57 impls; `Manifest`: 99 use sites). This is not a "traits are overused here" culture problem — it is a specific, enumerable set of 7 traits plus 3 non-trait equivalents, all deletable.

---

## 1. Pattern Index

| # | Pattern | Findings | On release/publish path | Fix cost | Risk if left | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B** | No shared *reader* for "what does this manifest say" — ecosystem dispatch re-hand-rolled per call site | 6 | **Yes (crash)** | M | **High** | **1** |
| **C** | Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline coexist; the live one re-typed the dead one's commands and lost capability | 3 | **Yes** | M | **High** | **2** |
| **D** | Fixed/linked group severity algebra has no owning type | 2 (+1) | **Yes (prior incident)** | M | **High** | **3** |
| **G** | Shared *primitives* are exported; shared *compositions* are not | 3 (5+3+1 copies) | Partly (publish stderr) | **S** | Med-High (security) | **4** |
| **A** | Speculative seams: abstraction built for a second consumer that never arrived | 10 | No | **S** | Low (comprehension tax) | **5** |
| **E** | Derive-twice instead of pass-the-value (preview vs. apply, CLI vs. report) | 4 | Partly | M | Med (this is the incident's shape) | **6** |
| **F** | Domain identifiers are raw `String`, so validation is a call-site concern and diverges | 2 (+1) | Yes (attestation, tags) | M | Med | **7** |
| **H** | Parallel arms hand-written over a closed set of kinds | 6 | No | **L** | Low-Med | **8** |

Findings map 1:1 onto patterns; a few carry a secondary pattern, noted inline.

---

## 2. Pattern B — No shared manifest *reader*; ecosystem dispatch re-hand-rolled

**Priority 1.** 6 instances, one of them a live panic on the release critical path.

### Instances

| Site | What it re-derives |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:277-308` | package version from a git blob (`manifest_version_at`) — **panics**; no Cargo workspace-inheritance, no Flit fallback |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:74-146` | package *name* from all three manifests — missing Flit's `tool.flit.metadata.module`, so Flit packages are silently undiscovered |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/locator.rs:104-208` | "which ecosystem is this project" — three semantics in one crate pair (multi-push in `projects()`, first-match in `declared_edges()`, membership-filtered in `IgnoreWalkLocator`) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:34-114` & `:511-582` | workspace-membership tables per ecosystem (also Pattern H) |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs:15-57` vs `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:86-139` | `napi.targets` — silently-drop vs. hard-error, divergence documented and left in place |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:22-30`, `:193-200`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:652-666` | `Package` → `ReleasePackageId` via `canonical_manifests()` (×3) |

### Root cause

The canonical knowledge already exists and is correct — it just isn't *reachable* from where these callers stand:

- `ManifestFormat` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:123-210`) already owns `file_name()`, `from_path()`, `ecosystem()`. **But there is no `ManifestFormat::ALL`**, so no caller can loop over ecosystems — everyone writes `if root.join("Cargo.toml").exists() { … } else if …`. Six `src/` files independently branch on all three manifest filenames.
- `callisto-manifests` readers are **path-and-`OpenContext`-only**: `CargoToml::open(decl, ctx)`, `PackageJson::open`, `PyprojectToml::open`. A caller holding a *string* (a `git show` blob, a walker's pre-read buffer) has no supported way in, so it re-parses by hand — and hand-parsing is where the panicking `[]` indexing and the missing fallbacks come from.

### Structural fix

1. **Add the enumeration.** `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL: [ManifestFormat; N]` + `Ecosystem::canonical_formats()`. Rewrite `ignore_walk.rs`, `locator.rs` (moon), `membership.rs`, `matrix.rs`, `napi.rs` to iterate the array instead of writing three `.exists()` checks. A new ecosystem then lights up all discovery paths at once, which is the current unstated (and unmet) expectation.
2. **Add a source-level read seam to `callisto-manifests`.** Either per-type `from_source(path: &Path, source: &str, ctx: &OpenContext) -> Result<Self, ManifestError>` (with `open` becoming `read_to_string` + `from_source`), or a free function:
   ```rust
   pub fn read_identity(format: ManifestFormat, source: &str) -> Result<ManifestIdentity, ManifestError>
   // { name: Option<String>, version: Option<VersionSource> }  // VersionSource::{Literal, InheritedFromWorkspace}
   ```
   `manifest_version_at` becomes a `git show` + one call. ## 3. Pattern C — Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline

**Priority 2.** 3 instances. The *newer* path is the live one and it is the *less* capable one.

### Instances

| New (live) | Old (richer, effectively dead) | What the live path lost |
|---|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:287-394` (`dispatch_registry`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs:172-283, 347-457, 477-528` | cargo: no `--locked`, no on-disk-version-vs-plan check; npm: **no pnpm/yarn/bun detection — plain `npm publish` in every workspace**; pypi: temp-dir build + upload-everything vs. `dist/` + normalized-name glob |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:424-469` (`dispatch_tag`) | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:437-465` (`GitAccess::create_tag`) | no `--` argv separator before the tag name (the old one has it, with a comment saying why); conversely the old one lacks `--no-sign` |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs:87-103` | `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/plan_publish.rs:12-25` | nothing — identical pipeline, one has a banner and a deprecation `eprintln!` |

Verified: `PublishOrchestrator`/`SubprocessRegistryClient` are constructed **only** inside `publish.rs`'s own `mod tests`. So this is not "two live paths drifting" — it is "the live path was rewritten from scratch against a tested reference implementation and silently dropped four behaviors." The pnpm one is a real breakage today for any pnpm/yarn workspace, and this repo's own discovery code supports `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

### Root cause

The durable-release rewrite (SPEC-RELEASE-\*) introduced a new execution model (permits, prepared effects, idempotent dispatch) and, because the old code was entangled with the old *orchestration*, reimplemented the *command construction* along with it. Command construction is the part with no orchestration content at all — it is a pure function from (ecosystem, plan, options) to an argv.

### Structural fix

1. **Extract an argv layer.** One module, e.g. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs`:
   ```rust
   pub struct Argv { pub program: String, pub args: Vec<String>, pub cwd: PathBuf }
   pub fn publish_argv(target: &PublishTarget, pkg: &PlannedPackage, ws: &WorkspaceFacts) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError>;
   pub fn tag_argv(name: &TagName, target: &CommitSha, annotation: &str) -> Argv;
   ```
   Pure, no `CommandRunner`, snapshot-testable — `insta`-style assertions on exact argv per (ecosystem × package manager × registry) combination. Both `dispatch_registry` and any surviving orchestrator call it. The pnpm/yarn/bun detection and `--locked` come back for free because the snapshot tests encode them.
2. **`dispatch_tag` calls `GitAccess::create_tag`**, extended with a `sign: bool`/`TagSignPolicy` parameter so `--no-sign` and `--` coexist. `release.rs` already imports `callisto_vcs::GitAccess` (line 17, used at line 140) — the reuse path is one import away.
3. **Decide the fate of `PublishOrchestrator` explicitly.** Either delete it and its 20 tests (they currently test a code path no user reaches — a false confidence signal), or make `callisto publish` the thin deprecated alias of `plan-publish` it already is (`publish::handle` → `plan_publish::handle` + banner) and keep the orchestrator only if it is going to be promoted.

### Enforcement

Arch test: the string literals `"cargo"`, `"npm"`, `"pnpm"`, `"yarn"`, `"bun"`, `"twine"`, `"git"` may appear as a subprocess *program name* only inside the argv module and `callisto-vcs`. Grep-shaped, cheap, and it is exactly the boundary that was crossed.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — silently wrong publish tool on pnpm/yarn workspaces is a production failure, not a maintenance hazard.

## 4. Pattern D — Group severity algebra has no owning type

**Priority 3.** This is the pattern that already caused the incident that triggered this audit.

### Instances

- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:362-502` — `union_fixed` / `union_linked`, **with** a stale-member guard (skip + `UnknownPackage` diagnostic, comment naming the `MissingField` crash it prevents)
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:303-405` — inline Linked block (304-363) and Fixed block (365-405), **without** that guard; the Linked block's per-member `bump_target(id, max_sev, &input)` reaches `input.base.get(id).ok_or(MissingField)` at `cascade.rs:417-419`
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:97-140` — `fixed_group_target` recomputes the same max-severity loop a third time, called *by* `cascade.rs` after `cascade.rs` has already computed `max_sev` itself
- (secondary) `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:70-125, 127-222` — fixed/linked arms duplicated in `validate_syntactic` and `resolve` (also Pattern H)

### Root cause

"Max severity across a group, propagated back to members" is a property of `GroupTable`, but it lives as a procedure inside whichever *phase* needs it (aggregate-time, cascade-convergence-time, target-resolution-time). Each phase re-derives it because `GroupTable` exposes only `members()` — an iterator — rather than the operation. The safety guard that one phase learned (skip members absent from `base_versions`) could not propagate to the others because there was nothing shared to attach it to.

### Structural fix

Move the algebra onto the type that owns the data:

```rust
impl GroupTable {
    /// Single definition of fixed/linked severity union, including the
    /// stale-member policy. Returns per-member targets plus diagnostics.
    pub fn union_severity(
        &self,
        kind: GroupKind,
        base: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Version>,
        severities: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>,
    ) -> (BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>, Vec<Diagnostic>);
}
```

`aggregate.rs` calls it once pre-cascade; `cascade.rs`'s two blocks call it inside the convergence loop; `fixed_group_target` is deleted (its caller already has `max_sev`). The stale-member guard now exists once, so the `MissingField` crash class disappears for Linked groups as well as Fixed.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `GroupDef::members()` may be called only from `groups.rs`. That is the structural statement "group semantics live in one module," and it is checkable. Add a property test asserting `aggregate → cascade` is idempotent for a workspace containing a group member that is absent from `base_versions` — the exact shape that crashes today.

**Cost:** M. **Risk of leaving it:** high — reachable crash plus demonstrated incident history.

### Instances

1. **Credential redaction, 5 copies** of the identical one-liner `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`:

   **Supporting evidence:** `callisto-moon` has *zero* redaction call sites (`rg redact crates/callisto-moon` → no hits) while constructing `CommandOutput`/`CommandError` from raw subprocess stderr (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs:30`, `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-moon/src/runner_pdk.rs:91`). The sixth crate simply never wrote the copy — which is what "composition by convention" produces.
2. **Glob compile-and-filter, 3 copies:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs:257-276` (inline), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs:319-326` (`compile_glob`, not called by its own crate-sibling), `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:41-56` (kept in sync *by comment*).
3. **Diagnostic line format:** `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs:132-142` re-inlines `render_diagnostics`' body (`:11-19`) that five sibling renderers call.

Same for `Glob::new → compile_matcher → map_err(InvalidGlob) → filter`.

### Structural fix — put the composition on the type that carries the data

```rust
// callisto-model/src/exec.rs
impl CommandOutput {
    /// stderr with known credential values redacted. Prefer over `.stderr`
    /// anywhere the text can reach a user-facing error or log.
    pub fn redacted_stderr(&self) -> String { … }
}

Then make the safe path the *shortest* path: make `CommandOutput.stderr` a private field with `raw_stderr()` (loud name) and `redacted_stderr()` accessors. The five locals delete themselves; `callisto-moon` gets redaction it never had; a new crate cannot forget.

Glob: one `TagGlob::compile(pattern) -> Result<TagMatcher, VcsError>` in `callisto-vcs`, re-exported; `callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` imports it and deletes its comment-enforced copy. `render_validate` calls `render_diagnostics`.

### Enforcement

Arch test: `known_credential_env_values` may be referenced only in `callisto-model`. Field privacy handles the rest via the compiler.

**Cost:** S. **Risk of leaving it:** medium-high — it is a credential-leak surface maintained by copy-paste, with one crate already missing the copy.

pub struct GitHubRepository { owner: String, repo: String }   // private fields
impl GitHubRepository {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, InvalidGitHubRepository>; // one charset, one rule
    pub fn as_slug(&self) -> String;   // "owner/repo"

Do the same for `TagName`: private field + `TagName::parse` rejecting leading `-`, control chars, and git's `check-ref-format` illegal sequences. **Enforcement:** the type system — an unvalidated slug becomes unconstructible.

**Cost:** M (a mechanical type substitution across ~8 fields plus serde round-trip tests). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — the looser validator guards the more security-sensitive boundary, which is the wrong way round.

### Structural fix — introduce the missing *values*, not a code-sharing scheme

The reason these copies exist is that the thing varying (a group kind, a rule kind, an ecosystem's membership table, a requirement string) has no representation, so the variation is expressed as code structure.

1. **PEP 508 gets a type.** `struct Requirement { name, extras, op_and_spec, marker }` with `parse` / `render` and a round-trip property test. 2. **TOML decor gets a helper.** `fn set_preserving_decor(item: &mut Item, key: &str, value: Value)` + `fn set_dependency_version(item: &mut Item, v: &str) -> Result<(), ManifestError>` handling the three shapes once. `CargoToml` and `WorkspaceCargoResolver` both call it; the extensive decor test suite in that file then covers one implementation instead of two.
3. **Kind becomes a parameter.** `GroupTable::resolve` takes `GroupKind` and loops `[Fixed, Linked]`; `ResolvedConfig::load` gets `fn resolve_package_config(raw: &RawPackageCommon, kind_label: &str) -> Result<PackageConfig, ConfigError>` called by both loops, so a new `PackageConfig` field is a compile error in exactly one place.
4. **Membership becomes generic.** `struct Membership { members, exclude, hybrid_root }` + `fn read_membership(root, spec: &MembershipSpec)` where `MembershipSpec` names the file and the TOML path. Pairs naturally with Pattern B's `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL`.
5. `write.rs::prepend`: compute `rest` in the if/else, then one shared tail.

## 10. Priority Ranking & Suggested Sequencing

| Rank | Pattern | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **B** — manifest reader | Contains the only *live crash* (§New Evidence), plus a silent discovery gap for Flit packages. On the release verification path. Fix is additive (new constructors, new const) before it is subtractive. |
| 2 | **C** — two pipeline generations | The live publish path is missing `--locked`, the on-disk version check, and package-manager detection. A pnpm workspace publishes with the wrong tool **today**. Also the tag-injection guard is on the dead path only. |
| 3 | **D** — group algebra | Already caused a production incident in this exact area; a reachable `MissingField` crash remains for Linked groups. Bounded, three call sites. |
| 4 | **G** — compositions | Hours of work; removes a five-way-copied security control and gives `callisto-moon` redaction it currently lacks entirely. |
| 5 | **A** — dead seams | 10 instances, near-zero behavioral risk, and it is the pattern most likely to keep recurring silently. Do it as one deletion PR plus the census test. |
| 6 | **E** — derive-twice | No live bug, but structurally identical to the incident; `tag.rs` preview/write is the one worth fixing first. |
| 7 | **F** — raw String identity | Security-adjacent; the weaker validator guards the attestation boundary. Medium cost, no urgency signal. |
| 8 | **H** — parallel arms | Largest volume, smallest observed divergence, highest regression risk. Take the two with correctness content (PEP 508, TOML decor); defer the rest. |

**Suggested workstreams (not 8 sequential PRs):**

- **W1 — "Release path single source of truth" (B + C + D).** These three share reviewers, tests, and blast radius, and together they close every high-severity finding. Order inside: B's `from_source` seam → D's `GroupTable::union_severity` → C's argv extraction. Land the `manifest_version_at` panic fix *first and alone* as a hotfix.
- **W2 — "Delete the decorations" (A + G).** One deletion PR (A) + one hardening PR (G). Small, independent, safe to run in parallel with W1.
- **W3 — "Plan values and parsed identities" (E + F).** Follows W1 naturally since both touch the same modules.
- **W4 — opportunistic (H).** Only when the surrounding file is already being modified.

**Enforcement summary — the four arch tests that make five of the eight patterns non-recurring.** All are grep- or census-shaped and belong in one `just arch-check` recipe wired into `ci-fast`:

1. Manifest filename literals & raw manifest parsing confined to `callisto-model` + `callisto-manifests` (kills B).
2. Subprocess program names confined to the argv module + `callisto-vcs` (kills C).
3. `GroupDef::members()` confined to `groups.rs` (kills D).
4. Every `pub trait` has ≥2 impls or a polymorphic use, else allowlisted with a reason (kills A).
   Plus, by the type system rather than a test: private fields on `CommandOutput.stderr`, `TagName.0`, and a new `GitHubRepository` (kill G and F).

---

## 11. New Evidence (escalations beyond the 32 findings)

**E1 — `manifest_version_at` panics; it does not fail closed. (Escalates finding #4 to critical.)**

`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:286-303` uses `toml_edit`'s `Index` impl:

```rust
.and_then(|document| document["package"]["version"].as_str().map(str::to_owned)),
…
document["project"]["version"].as_str()
    .or_else(|| document["tool"]["poetry"]["version"].as_str())
```

`toml_edit` 0.22.27's `impl Index<&str> for Table` is `self.get(key).expect("index not found")` (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/toml_edit-0.22.27/src/index.rs:102-107`), and `DocumentMut`'s forwards to it. Confirmed empirically with a scratch binary against the same crate version — all three panic:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Poetry-only `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.poetry]`, no `[project]`) | `panicked at 'index not found'` |
| PEP 621 `[project]` with `dynamic = ["version"]` | `panicked at 'index not found'` |
| `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]` and no `[package]` | `panicked at 'index not found'` |

Reachability: `derive_release_commit_decision` (`release_decision.rs:207-219`) calls `manifest_version_at` **unconditionally, for every canonical manifest of every package in the graph, at both the parent and the release commit** — not just packages being released. So one Poetry-managed Python package anywhere in the workspace aborts release-commit verification with a panic instead of the intended `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale`.

Contrast with the canonical reader it duplicates, `PyprojectToml::current_version` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:135-158`), which uses safe `.get()` chains, has the Poetry *and* Flit fallbacks, and returns a typed `ManifestError::MissingField`. This is the single clearest argument for Pattern B's fix.

A survey of the whole workspace found **no other panicking manifest index** in production code: `python.rs:204` and `init.rs:82,88` are `IndexMut` (inserting, safe), and `membership.rs:273` is `yaml_rust2`, whose `Index` returns `BadValue` rather than panicking (documented at `membership.rs:265-268`).

**E2 — `callisto-moon` has no redaction at all.** `rg redact crates/callisto-moon` returns zero hits, while `runner.rs:30` and `runner_pdk.rs:91` construct `CommandOutput` from raw subprocess stderr. Not a confirmed leak (no user-facing error formatting found there yet), but it demonstrates the failure mode of Pattern G: the convention doesn't propagate to a crate that never learned it.

---

## 12. Borderline / Flag for Human Triage (do not act unilaterally)

1. **Is Pattern C duplication or dead code?** `PublishOrchestrator`/`SubprocessRegistryClient` are constructed only in tests, and `callisto publish` is documented as a dry-run compatibility preview. Deleting them removes ~20 passing tests; keeping them keeps a richer reference implementation. **Decision needed from the owner: promote or delete.** Either way, extract the argv layer first — that part is unambiguous.
2. **`--no-sign` vs `--` in tag creation (finding #6).** These may be *deliberately* different: `--no-sign` matters in CI where `commit.gpgsign` is set globally (this repo's own test-hang history involves global gpgsign). Unifying must **keep** `--no-sign` and **add** `--`, not pick one implementation. Confirm with the release owner before collapsing.
3. **Tightening `is_safe_github_repository` (finding #3)** is a behavior change on a validation boundary. GitHub's own charset matches the stricter rule, but a repo slug that currently passes and would then fail is a hard error at `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::new`. Ship with a changeset and a migration note.
4. **Removing public items is `cargo semver-checks`-visible** (`just check-api`). `ChangesetStorage`, `last_tag_for`, `GitVcsProvider`, `PackageIdentityResolver`, `ReportPresenter`, `ManifestCstEditor` are all `pub` on published 0.6 crates. Needs an explicit policy call (proposed in §6) before the deletion PR lands.
5. **`ManifestCstEditor` is named in a spec.** `.claude/specs/SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001.json`'s reasoning trail explicitly covers it in AC-014 while noting it has zero callers. Deleting it needs a spec amendment, not just a code PR.
6. **`skip_publish_precheck` is public CLI surface** (`cli.rs:215-221`), and its help text describes an "already published?" check — a *different* feature from the dead `check_credentials`. Removing the flag is a user-visible CLI break; implementing it is new work. Product decision, not a cleanup.
7. **Finding #9's crash claim is precise for Linked groups only.** The Fixed-group path routes through `fixed_group_target`, which has a soft fallback rather than the `MissingField` panic. The duplication and the guard asymmetry are real for both; the crash is demonstrated for Linked.
8. **Finding #29's `declared_edges` comparison isn't apples-to-apples.** `IgnoreWalkLocator` doesn't implement `declared_edges` at all (it takes the trait default `None`, `locate/mod.rs:14-16`), and its "Cargo-before-npm" test pins *sort order*, not exclusivity — it still returns both ecosystems. The well-supported half is `projects()`: membership filtering exists in one locator and not the other. Also a genuine product question: **should** the moon locator apply Cargo/npm/uv membership filtering, or does moon own project boundaries by design? Answer that before unifying.
9. **Finding #8 (`ReleasePackageId` ×3) is currently consistent**, and the `release.rs` variant's extra ecosystem-presence filter is intentional. Low value on its own; fold it into Pattern B's work rather than as a standalone PR.
10. **Finding #22 (`has_changesets`)** — verify no intentional difference between the JSON field and the `--check` semantics (e.g. a package category deliberately excluded from one) before switching the CLI to read the field. Very likely a one-line fix, but confirm with a test that asserts the two agree."

a Cargo.toml with no [package] table aborted release-commit
verification with a panic instead of the intended

fix(graph): stop manifest_version_at from panicking on missing tables

content.text:
Committed and pushed to PR #54.

## Critical finding fixed, now in PR #54

The audit's synthesis surfaced something I verified independently before trusting it: my own `manifest_version_at` (written today, for the persist-and-verify fix) used `toml_edit`'s panicking `Index` operator instead of safe `.get()` chains. I reproduced the panic myself against the exact pinned `toml_edit` version, then fixed it and added two regression tests (one proving no-panic on the previously-crashing shapes, one proving the existing Poetry-fallback and normal-Cargo behavior still works). Clean build, clippy, and tests — now pushed.

## Audit results

12 parallel agents scanned the whole workspace, merged to 32 findings, all 32 survived adversarial verification, then a synthesis pass grouped them into **8 architectural patterns**, ranked by priority:

| # | Pattern | Findings | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | No shared manifest *reader* — every crate hand-parses Cargo.toml/package.json/pyproject.toml itself | 6 | **1** (contains the panic just fixed, plus a silent discovery gap for Flit-based Python packages) |
| C | Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline coexist; the live one is *less* capable than the dead one | 3 | **2** (a pnpm/yarn workspace publishes with the wrong tool **today**) |
| D | Fixed/linked group severity math implemented 3x — this is the exact bug class that started this whole session | 2 | **3** (a reachable crash remains for linked groups) |
| G | Credential redaction copy-pasted into 5 crates; a 6th (`callisto-moon`) never got the copy at all | 3 | 4 (security-adjacent, cheap fix) |
| A | 7 traits + 3 config structs are dead abstraction — zero implementations/callers beyond their own definition | 10 | 5 (pure deletion, near-zero risk) |
| E | "Preview vs. write" branches re-derive instead of reusing the same computed value | 4 | 6 |
| F | GitHub repo/tag identity validated inconsistently across call sites (one validator is stricter than the other) | 2 | 7 |
| H | Config/membership parsing duplicated per-kind (package vs package-set, Cargo vs Python) | 6 | 8 |

Full report (structural fixes, workstream sequencing, and a "borderline — needs your call" section for things like whether to delete the dead `PublishOrchestrator` or promote it) is in the workflow transcript. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
3	# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
4	#
5	# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
6	# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
7	# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
8	# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
9	# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
10	# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
11	# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
12	# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
13	# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
17	
18	# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
19	# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
20	# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
21	# commit API, on the staging branch.
22	base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
23	
24	release_pr_snapshot() {
25	  local raw_prs
26	  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
27	  jq -cn \
28	    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
29	    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
30	    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
31	    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
32	    '{
33	      schemaVersion: 2,
34	      repository: $repository,
35	      baseBranch: $base_branch,
36	      baseCommit: $base_commit,
37	      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
38	        number,
39	        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
40	        headBranch: .headRefName,
41	        headCommit: .headRefOid
42	      }]
43	    }'
44	}
45	
46	snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
47	decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
48	  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
49	  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
50	  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
51	  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
52	decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
53	
54	case "$decision_kind" in
55	  noop)
56	    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
57	    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
58	    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
59	    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
60	    exit 0
61	    ;;
62	  create)
63	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
64	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
65	    existing_pr=''
66	    ;;
67	  update)
68	    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
69	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
70	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
71	    ;;
72	  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
73	esac
74	
75	echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
76	if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
77	  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
78	  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
79	else
80	  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
81	fi
82	
83	read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
84	"${command[@]}"
85	git add -A
86	test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }
87	
88	plan_file=$(mktemp)
89	callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
90	local_tree=$(git write-tree)
91	
92	staging_created=false
93	cleanup_staging() {
94	  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
95	    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
96	      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
97	  fi
98	  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
99	}
100	trap cleanup_staging EXIT
101	
102	# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
103	# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
104	# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
105	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
106

108	  :
109	else
110	  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
111	fi
112	staging_created=true
113	
114	jq -n \

116	  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
117	  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
118	  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
119	  '{
120	    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
121	    variables: {
122	      input: {
123	        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
124	        message: {headline: $headline},
125	        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
126	        fileChanges: {
127	          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
128	          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
129	        }
130	      }
131	    }
132	  }' > body.json
133	
134	new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
135	remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
136	if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
137	  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
138	  exit 1
139	fi
140	
141	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
142	
143	if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
144	  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
145	else
146	  if ! gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
147	    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
148	  fi
149	fi
150	moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
151	if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
152	  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
153	  exit 1
154	fi
155	
156	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
157	
158	label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
159	if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
160	  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
161	fi
162	
163	case "$decision_kind" in
164	  create)
165	    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
166	    ;;
167	  update)
168	    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
169	    ;;
